issue_title: caveman-shrink: "make sure" / "be sure" collapse to "make" / "be" — is dropping "sure" inside those collocations intended?
issue_description:
`src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/compress.js` lists `sure` in `PLEASANTRIES`, so it is removed wherever it stands alone. That is right for "Sure, this returns the value", but the same rule fires inside "make sure" and "be sure", where "sure" is not a pleasantry but the verb's object. The result is an instruction with a hole in it.

**Reproduce** (current `main`):
```
node -e 'const {compress}=require("./src/mcp-servers/caveman-shrink/compress.js");
for (const t of ["Make sure the file exists.","Make sure to call init before any other tool.","Be sure to pass an absolute path.","Not sure why this fails."]) console.log(JSON.stringify(t),"=>",JSON.stringify(compress(t).compressed));'
```
```
"Make sure the file exists."                    => "Make file exists."
"Make sure to call init before any other tool." => "Make to call init before any other tool."
"Be sure to pass an absolute path."             => "Be to pass absolute path."
"Not sure why this fails."                      => "Not why this fails."
```

In the first case the meaning is inverted, not just weakened: "Make sure the file exists" is a check, while "Make file exists" reads as "create the file".

**Why it matters**
`compressDescriptionsInPlace` rewrites MCP tool descriptions on `tools/list`, so "Make to call init before any other tool" is what the model reads as the tool's contract. "Make sure to X first" is one of the most common phrasings in tool descriptions (the existing test `compresses real MCP-style description` uses "Please make sure to provide the location as a city name" as its sample input, though it only asserts that "city name" survives). This goes against the spirit of CONTRIBUTING's rule that compressors must never silently corrupt a payload, and it has the same shape as the hyphenated-compound corruption fixed in #1055 (`just-in-time` → `-in-time`): a word that is a filler on its own is not a filler inside a fixed collocation.

**Question**
Is removing "sure" inside "make sure" / "be sure" / "not sure" intended, or should the pleasantry rule skip those collocations (e.g. a negative lookbehind for `make|be|not`, or keeping "sure" only when it is sentence-initial and followed by a comma)? Happy to send a PR with a regression test once the intended behaviour is confirmed. The same question applies to the hedge `might` ("might be null" → "be null"), but that one at least drops a hedge rather than the object of a verb, so I am raising only the "sure" case here.

issue_title: pi extension reuses one original base URL across models in the same provider
issue_description:
**What happen**

Pi supports a separate `baseUrl` for each model in one provider.

`ProviderRouter` stores one original base URL for each provider. This sequence can route a custom model to the wrong endpoint:

1. The user selects an `openai` model that uses `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
2. Caveman stores that URL and applies a provider-wide gateway override.
3. Pi reports the gateway URL for all `openai` models.
4. The user selects another `openai` model with a custom model-level `baseUrl`.
5. Caveman reuses the first model URL and routes the custom model to the OpenAI proxy route.

The second model can target a local relay, Azure, or another custom endpoint. Its request can reach the wrong service.

This behavior exists on `main`. PR #972 fixes provider-level custom endpoints, but it does not fix this model-level case.

**Expected**

Caveman must preserve the original URL for each model before it applies a provider-wide override. The registry cannot supply these URLs after the override.

If a model has a custom endpoint, Caveman must keep that model direct and show the pass-through notice.

The regression test must register two models under the same provider. One model uses the default endpoint, and one uses a custom endpoint.

The test must route the default model first. Then it must select the custom model and make sure that the model stays direct.

The test must select the default model again and make sure that routing resumes.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: pi provider "openai" has one default model and one model with a custom baseUrl
Got:   after the default model routes, the custom model also routes to api.openai.com
Want:  the custom model stays direct, and the default model routes through Caveman
```

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [x] Other: Pi

**Version / install method**

Current `main` with `@caveman-ai/pi`, pinned to Pi 0.84.2. This behavior exists before PR #972.

PR #972 fixes provider-level custom endpoints. It does not fix model-level custom endpoints in the same provider.

issue_title: Website benchmark caption says medians, but source report uses means
issue_description:
## Summary

The benchmark caption on https://ponytail.dev/#numbers calls the displayed results **medians**, while the repository's report describes the same results as **means**. This makes the published aggregation method inconsistent even though the headline percentages agree.

## Reproduction

Observed on 2026-09-04:

1. Open the official homepage's benchmarks section. It displays 54% less code, 22% fewer tokens, 20% lower cost, and 27% faster, with the caption `medians across 12 feature tasks on a FastAPI + React repo`.
2. Compare [the agentic report's summary](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/blob/974d940a1c5344210874150b98ff0d2c861fab6a/benchmarks/results/2026-06-18-agentic.md#summary-percent-change-vs-baseline-all-metrics): it describes the aggregation as a mean across each tier's tasks, with every task averaged over four runs, and lists the same four percentages.
3. The README also explicitly describes the 54% figure as a mean; merged #165 clarified the distinction between that average and the per-task peak.

## Expected / actual

Expected: the website uses the same aggregation label as the linked repository methodology (mean/average), or links a separate median-based analysis if that is the intended source.

Actual: the live caption says median while the repository's source report says mean. These statistics are not interchangeable, so readers cannot tell which methodology the site is advertising.

This report concerns the caption, not a challenge to the measured percentages. No model/API benchmark was rerun.

## Scope

I could not find the deployed website source among the 159 tracked files at current main `974d940a1c5344210874150b98ff0d2c861fab6a`, so there is no safe in-repository patch to attach. The source report should not be changed merely to match the website. Existing #454 establishes this repository as a place for official-site corrections. Searches for `ponytail.dev`, `median`, `medians`, and `mean` found no equivalent caption report.

issue_title: bug: shell install command fails on `npm` >=12
issue_description:
**What happen**

Ran the [shell install command](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman#install) and it failed:

```log
npm error code EALLOWGIT
npm error Fetching packages of type "git" have been disabled
npm error Refusing to fetch "github:JuliusBrussee/caveman"
npm error A complete log of this run can be found in: /home/user/.npm/_logs/2026-07-11T14_01_09_335Z-debug-0.log
```

**Reason**

```bash
> npm -v
12.0.0
```

> - _allow-git and allow-remote now default to "none"; set them to "all" (or "root") to install git or user-supplied tarball-URL dependencies._

**[Source](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/changelog#%EF%B8%8F-breaking-changes)**

**Fix**

macOS · Linux · WSL · Git Bash
```bash
export NPM_CONFIG_ALLOW_GIT=all
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.sh | bash
unset NPM_CONFIG_ALLOW_GIT
```

Windows · PowerShell 5.1+
```pwsh
$env:NPM_CONFIG_ALLOW_GIT = "all"
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.ps1 | iex
Remove-Item Env:NPM_CONFIG_ALLOW_GIT
```

**Platform**
- [ ] Claude Code
- [x] Codex
- [x] Other: global (`~/.agents`)

**Version / install method**
Latest / [shell install command](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman#install)

issue_title: docs: multiple core sections outdated for 2025-2026 cloud-native practice
issue_description:
Hi maintainers — first, thank you for the primer. It's still the most-linked resource for system design interviews.

I consistently hitting gaps where the content reflects ~2015-2017 practices. These aren't nitpicks — they lead to wrong design choices in interviews today.

**Outdated / missing areas found by section:**

**1. Latency numbers (Appendix)**
- Still uses 2012 figures: L1 0.5ns, SSD random 150µs, 1Gbps network
- 2025 reality: L1 ~1ns, NVMe random ~20µs, 100Gbps datacenter RTT ~0.1-0.5ms, 1MB SSD sequential ~0.1ms (not 1ms). Candidates using old numbers are off by 10-100x on back-of-envelope.

**2. Load Balancer + CDN**
- Covers hardware LB, HAProxy, round-robin, Layer 4/7 only
- Missing: service mesh (Envoy/Istio) for east-west, global anycast, edge compute (Workers/Lambda@Edge), HTTP/3 QUIC, and cloud-managed LBs (ALB/NLB/Global Accelerator). No mention of connection-ID load balancing for QUIC.

**3. Database / NoSQL**
- Focuses on master-slave replication, MySQL query cache (removed in MySQL 8.0), and "graph DBs are new/not widely used"
- Missing entirely: Distributed SQL (Spanner, CockroachDB, Yugabyte), vector databases (pgvector, Pinecone), lakehouse (Iceberg/Delta), time-series DBs, and NewSQL consensus patterns. DynamoDB still labeled "document-oriented" only.

**4. Asynchronism & Communication**
- Message queues limited to Redis/RabbitMQ/SQS with no delivery semantics
- Kafka only in appendix, no partitions/retention; Pulsar missing
- No exactly-once, outbox pattern, or idempotency discussion
- RPC mentions Thrift/Protobuf but not gRPC; no GraphQL, WebSockets, or HTTP/3

**5. Security & Availability**
- Security section explicitly says "could use some updates" — still only "encrypt at rest, sanitize inputs"
- Missing: zero-trust, mTLS, OAuth2/OIDC, secrets management (Vault/KMS)
- Availability only covers active-passive and 2-node active-active; no multi-region active-active, chaos engineering, or SLO-based design
- Observability: only Dapper mentioned, no OpenTelemetry, traces/metrics/logs

**6. Application layer / Real-world**
- Examples are pre-2015 (Twitter 2013 architecture)
- No containers, Kubernetes, serverless, or service mesh

**Impact:** Junior engineers following the primer literally will design around RAID-style disks, master-slave MySQL, and hardware LBs — patterns that are red flags in 2025 FAANG/staff loops, where interviewers expect cloud-native defaults.

issue_title: Issue : Incorrect type hint in LinkedList class of query_cache_snippets.py
issue_description:
The `Cache` class' `get` and `set` methods refer to a member named `lookup` that is defined as a dictionary: `self.lookup = {}`. Therefore, the line `node = self.lookup[query]` will throw an exception if query is not present in the cache. The code should use `self.lookup.get(query)` instead which will return None instead of throwing an exception. Additionally, the Cache class refers to a member called `map` which is never defined. It is likely a typo and it should be `lookup`.

```python
class Cache(object):

    def __init__(self, MAX_SIZE):
        self.MAX_SIZE = MAX_SIZE
        self.size = 0
        self.lookup = {}
        self.linked_list = LinkedList()

    def get(self, query):
        """Get the stored query result from the cache.

        Accessing a node updates its position to the front of the LRU list.
        """
        node = self.lookup.get(query)
        if node is None:
            return None
        self.linked_list.move_to_front(node)
        return node.results

    def set(self, results, query):
        """Set the result for the given query key in the cache.

        When updating an entry, updates its position to the front of the LRU list.
        If the entry is new and the cache is at capacity, removes the oldest entry
        before the new entry is added.
        """
        node = self.lookup.get(query)
        if node is not None:
            # Key exists in cache, update the value
            node.results = results
            self.linked_list.move_to_front(node)
        else:
            # Key does not exist in cache
            if self.size == self.MAX_SIZE:
                # Remove the oldest entry from the linked list and lookup
                self.lookup.pop(self.linked_list.tail.query, None)
                self.linked_list.remove_from_tail()
            else:
                self.size += 1
            # Add the new key and value
            new_node = Node(query, results)
            self.linked_list.append_to_front(new_node)
            self.lookup[query] = new_node
```

issue_title: Simplify DSL fingerprint for resume guard (drop redundant canonicalization; decide field placement)
issue_description:
## Context
PR #17351 introduced a dual-fingerprint guard (`guardDSLChange`) so that editing a pipeline's DSL template between a failed run and its resume no longer errors out: a stale eino checkpoint is discarded when either the DSL-file fingerprint (`cpID:dsl`) or the runtime-override fingerprint (`cpID:ovf`) no longer matches.

## Finding: the canonicalization round-trip is redundant
`NewPipelineFromDSL` currently does `json.Marshal(canvasDSL)` to produce a "canonical" byte form before hashing. Investigation shows this is unnecessary for the canvas path:

- The canvas DSL is loaded from the DB (`user_canvas.dsl` longtext) into `entity.JSONMap` (`map[string]interface{}`). On read it is `json.Unmarshal`-ed (order lost), then `json.Marshal`-ed again in `loadDSLFromCanvas` (`internal/ingestion/task/pipeline_executor.go`). Go's `json.Marshal` sorts map keys, so the string reaching `NewPipelineFromDSL` is already deterministic.
- Built-in templates are read from static `.json` files; a formatting-only change there is a deliberate commit, and the false-positive cost is only a one-time fresh re-run.

## Open design question: where to compute the fingerprint / keep the field?
`Run` is called separately from `NewPipelineFromDSL`, so the DSL must be remembered somehow. Options:

- **Approach 1 (recommended):** compute `dslFP = sha256(dsl)` inside `NewPipelineFromDSL` and store `dslFP string` (instead of the current `rawDSL []byte`). No Run-time hashing, no full DSL bytes stored, caller has no extra responsibility.
- **Approach 2:** caller computes the fingerprint before `Run` and injects it (e.g. `WithDSLFingerprint` / setter). Keeps `NewPipelineFromDSL` a pure compiler but adds a "forgotten injection" failure mode.
- **Approach 3:** pass `dslFP` as a `Run` parameter (zero field) but changes `Run`'s signature across many call sites.
- Fieldless alternative considered: hash `json.Marshal(p.canvas)` at Run time. Rejected because it couples the fingerprint to `Canvas` struct serialization — renaming/reordering a `Canvas` json field would silently invalidate all existing checkpoints (one-time but self-healing false positive).

## Decision
Deferred — recorded for later.

issue_title: Windows auto-update can leave cuda_v12\ggml-cuda.dll as .tmp, causing 0 B VRAM / CPU fallback
issue_description:
### What is the issue?

On Windows, Ollama suddenly stopped detecting my NVIDIA GPU and fell back to CPU. The failure was ultimately traced to a missing `ggml-cuda.dll` in the installed CUDA backend after what appears to have been an automatic Ollama update.

Before the failure, `ollama --version` reported 0.34.4. During diagnosis, `ollama serve` reported version 0.35.0, suggesting the desktop app had updated during the session.

### Environment

- OS: Windows
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB
- CPU: Intel
- Ollama: 0.35.0 after update/reinstall
- Native Windows install (not Docker)
- A secondary RTX 2060 Super was physically removed during isolation testing

### Symptoms

`nvidia-smi` detected the RTX 5070 Ti normally and GPU benchmarks worked correctly, but Ollama reported no GPU and ran entirely on CPU:

```text
Available devices:
  (none)

inference compute id=cpu library=cpu
total_vram="0 B"
```

Explicitly forcing `cuda_v12` or Vulkan did not help while the installation was in this state.

### Important discovery

Inspecting:

```text
C:\Users\me\AppData\Local\Programs\Ollama\lib\ollama\cuda_v12
```

showed:

```text
concrt140.dll        311688
cublas64_12.dll   113720712
cublasLt64_12.dll 692449672
cudart64_12.dll      582024
is-FD36GKZTBY.tmp 349576072
```

Critically:

```powershell
Test-Path "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Ollama\lib\ollama\cuda_v12\ggml-cuda.dll"
```

returned:

```text
False
```

I then uninstalled/reinstalled Ollama **without deleting my model directory**.

After reinstall, the same directory contained:

```text
ggml-cuda.dll            349576072
```

and the previous `.tmp` file was gone.

The abandoned temporary file before reinstall was **349,576,072 bytes**, exactly the same size as the restored `ggml-cuda.dll`.

### Result after reinstall

GPU detection immediately worked again without changing the NVIDIA driver or GPU hardware:

```text
Available devices:
  CUDA0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (16275 MiB, 15037 MiB free)

ggml_cuda_init: found 1 CUDA devices (Total VRAM: 16275 MiB):
  Device 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti, compute capability 12.0, VMM: yes, VRAM: 16275 MiB

load_backend: loaded CUDA backend from C:\Users\me\AppData\Local\Programs\Ollama\lib\ollama\cuda_v12\ggml-cuda.dll

inference compute id=0 filter_id=0 library=CUDA compute=12.0 name=CUDA0 description="NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti" total="15.9 GiB" available="14.7 GiB"
```

### Suspected cause

The Windows updater/install process appears to have staged the CUDA backend DLL into a temporary file but failed to complete the rename/finalization step, leaving a partially updated CUDA backend directory.

Because `ggml-cuda.dll` was absent, Ollama started normally but GPU discovery found no devices and silently fell back to CPU.

### Suggested improvement

It may be worth having the Windows updater:

- verify required backend DLLs before considering an update complete;
- use an atomic replace/rollback strategy for backend files;
- refuse to finalize the update (or automatically repair) if `ggml-cuda.dll` is missing;
- surface a clearer error when CUDA runtime DLLs are present but the CUDA backend DLL itself is absent.

Possibly related: #12618, but this report identifies a specific missing backend file and a same-size abandoned `.tmp` file that was repaired by reinstall.

The authorize/consent page (route `/auth/authorize`, file `page.tsx`) treats the `redirectURI` query parameter as a trusted navigation target: **Deny** navigates to it verbatim via `window.location.href` (page.tsx:111-118, no scheme/host validation anywhere on the page); **Authorize** unconditionally follows `response.data.redirect_url` (:96-101, the product of the backend error branches). Setup: an OAuth app `poc-app` exists in the platform with the registered callback `https://registered-callback.example/real` — the only URL this app should ever be allowed to redirect a user to. issue_title: Built-in prompts inconsistently omit the "answer in the user's language" rule: /review, /init and subagents reply in English to a Chinese conversation
issue_description:
### Description

OpenCode already contains an instruction telling the model to answer in the user's language. At `v2.0.22` that sentence lives in exactly **two** prompts, and neither of them is one a user-facing command or a subagent actually runs under:

| Prompt file | Lines | Has a "same language as the user" rule |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/plugin/system-prompt/kimi.txt` | 95 | **yes — line 19** |
| `packages/core/src/plugin/agent.ts` (title/summary agents) | 156 | **yes — line 40** |
| `packages/core/src/plugin/system-prompt/trinity.txt` | 97 | no |
| `packages/core/src/plugin/system-prompt/meta.txt` | 55 | no |
| `packages/core/src/plugin/system-prompt/gpt-astra.txt` | 45 | no |
| `packages/core/src/plugin/system-prompt/gpt.txt` | 39 | no |
| `packages/core/src/plugin/system-prompt/anthropic.txt` | 2 | no |
| `packages/core/src/plugin/command/review.txt` | 100 | no |
| `packages/core/src/plugin/command/initialize.txt` | 65 | no |
| `packages/core/src/session/runner/prompt/system.txt` | 15 | no |
| `PROMPT_EXPLORE` (inside `packages/core/src/plugin/agent.ts`) | — | no |

The two that carry it are the two a user never sees: the Kimi model-family prompt, and the hidden `title`/`summary` maintenance agents. That is why a session title can come out in the user's language while the body of the same session comes out in English.

**1. `/review` and `/init` prepend an English-only prompt to the user's message.** `packages/core/src/plugin/command.ts`:

```ts
function append(template: string, input: string) {
  const value = input.trim()
  if (template.includes("$ARGUMENTS")) return template.replaceAll("$ARGUMENTS", () => value)
  return [template, value].filter(Boolean).join("\n\n")
}
```

```ts
text: append(PROMPT_REVIEW.replace("${path}", location.project.directory), input.prompt.text),
```

So all 100 lines of `review.txt` become the **start of the user message**, ahead of whatever the user typed. Someone typing `/review` in a Chinese session sends 100 lines of English-only instructions followed by a Chinese request, and nothing in that prompt mentions output language.

**2. The `general` subagent has no prompt of its own at all.** `packages/core/src/plugin/agent.ts`:

```ts
editor.update(Agent.ID.make("general"), (item) => {
  item.name = Agent.Name.make("General")
  item.description = "General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. ..."
  item.mode = "subagent"
  item.permissions.push(...)
})
```

There is no `item.system`, so there is nowhere for a language instruction to live. `explore` does get one (`item.system = PROMPT_EXPLORE`), and that prompt is English-only too.

**3. Five of the six model-family base prompts do not carry the rule**, so on `anthropic`, `gpt`, `gpt-astra`, `meta` and `trinity` the model is never told to follow the user's language. The only family that is told is `kimi`.

**Relation to #49889** — that issue asks for a user-facing configuration option to pin the model's language. This one asks for nothing new: the rule already exists in-tree, it is simply not applied to the prompts that actually run. I do not see a need for a config knob for behaviour the built-in prompts should already have.

**Suggested fix** — hoist the sentence into a single shared fragment and compose it into every prompt in the table above, `PROMPT_EXPLORE` included. No new user-facing surface and no behaviour change for anyone who writes in English.

### Steps to reproduce

Static, which is what I actually ran — tag `v2.0.22`, commit `527f0b931d1f9b3ebd34e106c51b31ce5db5b075`:

```bash
for f in packages/core/src/plugin/command/review.txt \
         packages/core/src/plugin/command/initialize.txt \
         packages/core/src/plugin/system-prompt/*.txt \
         packages/core/src/session/runner/prompt/system.txt; do
  printf '%-58s %s\n' "$f" "$(grep -ci 'same language' "$f")"
done
grep -n 'same language' packages/core/src/plugin/agent.ts
```

Observed: `kimi.txt` 1 hit, `agent.ts` line 40, everything else 0.

Behavioural, reported by a Chinese-speaking user on this version and **not independently reproduced by me** — both steps need the chat UI, which I cannot drive:

1. In a session where the conversation has been in Chinese, run `/review`. The review comes back in English.
2. In the same session, hand a subagent a task. Its answer comes back in English.

For the record, I did see one English subagent answer this session, but my task text was itself written in English with an English report skeleton, so that instance is explained by the input and I am not offering it as evidence of the defect.

### Screenshot and/or share link

None — the reproduction is file-level, so the line-level evidence above is the reproduction.

### Plugins

None — built-in prompts only.

### OpenCode version

`2.0.22`. The tag resolves directly to commit `527f0b931d1f9b3ebd34e106c51b31ce5db5b075` (checked via the GitHub API).

### Operating System

Windows (win32).

### Terminal

Windows PowerShell 5.1 (`powershell.exe`), which is the shell OpenCode spawns on this machine; ACP 936, `[Console]::OutputEncoding` is gb2312. Every file in the table was fetched from the API and scanned byte-exactly, so console decoding plays no part in the evidence above.

issue_title: [FEATURE REQUEST] <title> Add K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Classification Algorithm
issue_description:
### What would you like to Propose?

I propose adding a **K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)** implementation to the machinelearning package.

The machinelearning package was recently introduced and currently contains only a few supervised learning algorithms. K-Nearest Neighbors is one of the most fundamental machine learning algorithms and is commonly taught alongside Linear Regression and Naive Bayes in introductory machine learning courses. Adding it would naturally expand the package with another core classification algorithm.

KNN is a good fit for this repository because:

- It is one of the most widely used supervised learning algorithms for classification.
- It can be implemented entirely using standard Java (java.util) without any external dependencies, matching the educational and dependency-free style of this repository.
- The algorithm is straightforward to understand and demonstrates important concepts such as distance metrics, nearest-neighbor search, and majority voting.
- It complements the existing LinearRegression and MultinomialNaiveBayesClassifier implementations already present in the machinelearning package.

### Issue details

**Algorithm / problem statement:** Given a set of labeled training samples and a value of k, classify an unseen sample by computing its Euclidean distance to every training sample, selecting the k nearest neighbors, and assigning the class that receives the majority vote.

- src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/machinelearning/KNearestNeighbors.java

- Store training data through a fit() method.
- Predict the class of a single sample using Euclidean distance.
- Predict class labels for multiple samples.
- Majority-vote classification with deterministic tie-breaking (smaller class label wins).
- Input validation for:
  - k <= 0
  - null or empty datasets
  - inconsistent feature dimensions
  - mismatched feature/label counts
  - prediction before fitting

- src/test/java/com/thealgorithms/machinelearning/KNearestNeighborsTest.java

- Unit tests on well-separated datasets.
- Batch prediction tests.
- Tests for invalid inputs and exception handling.
- Tie-breaking behavior.
- Prediction before fitting.
- Dimension mismatch tests.

- The implementation will include Javadocs describing the algorithm, its time complexity (O(n · d + n log n) in this implementation because neighbors are sorted), and a reference to the Wikipedia article.

### Additional Information

I searched the repository and existing pull requests and could not find a K-Nearest Neighbors implementation in the Java repository. A previous pull request (#2484) titled "KNN Algorithm" was closed as invalid because it did not contain an actual KNN implementation.

If this proposal is accepted, I'd be happy to implement the algorithm along with comprehensive JUnit 5 tests and documentation following the repository's coding standards.

issue_title: [Bug]: Email gateway drops all PurelyMail senders — auth=pass Authentication-Results verdict unrecognized
issue_description:
### Bug Description

When using PurelyMail as the email provider, the Hermes email gateway drops every incoming message as "unauthenticated" even when the sender is in `EMAIL_ALLOWED_USERS` and `EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID` is correctly configured. The gateway never responds.

**Root Cause:**

PurelyMail stamps `Authentication-Results: purelymail.com; auth=pass` instead of the standard `dmarc=pass/spf=pass/dkim=pass` format. The email adapter's `_AUTH_METHOD_RE` regex in `plugins/platforms/email/adapter.py` only matches dmarc|spf|dkim methods, so `auth=pass` is parsed but the verdict is unrecognized — the sender-authentication check falls through to False and every sender from @purelymail.com is silently dropped  before authorization is even checked.

This affects any email provider that uses the non-standard **auth=pass** Authentication-Results token.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes email gateway with PurelyMail (or any provider that stips auth=pass)
2. Set EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID=purelymail.com
3. Set EMAIL_ALLOWED_USERS=email@purelymail.com
4. Send an email to the Hermes mailbox from email@purelymail.com
5. Observe in gateway.log:

[Email] Dropping sender with unauthenticated From: emial@purelymail.com (authentication failed (purelymail.com; auth=pass)).

The sender is never dispatched to the agent.

### Expected Behavior

When authserv_id is pinned to the receiving MTA and the Authentication-Results header contains auth=pass from that trusted source, the sender should be authenticated and dispatched like dmarc=pass senders.

### Actual Behavior

Senders are dropped with authentication failed (purelymail.com; auth=pass) even though authserv_id is configured and matches.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
hermes:          0.21.5+6977.gaf90026.dirty [af90026a] (2026-10-04)
os:              Linux 7.1.1-76070101-generic x86_64

issue_title: Empty response with finish_reason "length" and zero tokens is treated as success
issue_description:
## Summary

When a provider returns a well-formed but empty stream (`finish_reason: "length"`, `content: ""`, no usage), opencode ends the turn with no message and no error. The user sees no output and no error, and the run exits successfully. This makes provider-side failures impossible to diagnose from the TUI/CLI.

I hit this with OpenAI GPT-family models via OpenRouter whenever a tool schema contained `"enum": []`. The bad tool schema is the root trigger (reported separately to the MCP server), but opencode should not treat a degenerate empty response as a successful completion.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an OpenRouter provider and a remote MCP server that exposes a tool with `"enum": []` in its parameters.

   Minimal: a single tool whose parameter schema is `{"type": "string", "enum": []}`.

2. Run:

   ```
   opencode run -m openrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna "What is the capital of France?"
   ```

3. Observe: no output, no error, exit success.

   The same request without the empty `enum` returns a normal answer.

## Expected

Either a normal answer, or an explicit error such as:

```
model returned no content (finish reason: length)
```

## Actual

The stored assistant message is degenerate:

- `finish: "length"`
- `tokens.input: 0`, `tokens.output: 0`, `tokens.reasoning: 0`
- parts contain only `step-start` and `step-finish`

The loop exits quietly with no user-visible error:

```
message=stream providerID=openrouter modelID=openai/gpt-6-luna
message="llm runtime selected" llm.runtime=ai-sdk llm.provider=openrouter llm.model=openai/gpt-6-luna
message=loop session.id=... step=1
message="exiting loop" session.id=...
```

Raw provider response:

```
data: {"id":"gen-...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","model":"openai/gpt-6-luna","provider":"OpenAI","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"","role":"assistant"},"finish_reason":"length","native_finish_reason":"max_output_tokens"}]}
data: [DONE]
```

## Suggested fixes

1. **Surface an error for empty completions.** When a step finishes with `finishReason = "length"`, zero output tokens, and no content, raise a visible error instead of completing successfully. Right now it is indistinguishable from a valid (if terse) answer.

2. **Sanitize outgoing tool schemas.** Strip empty `enum` arrays (and other invalid JSON Schema constructs) before sending tools to a provider. opencode builds the tool list, so it is the right place to defend against malformed MCP schemas. This would have prevented the failure entirely.

## Environment

- opencode 1.18.32, Linux
- Provider `openrouter` (`@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider` 2.9.0)
- Model `openai/gpt-6-luna` (reproduces with other OpenAI GPT models)

issue_title: Language server retains the pre-edit program and its checkers for the rest of the session after the first edit
issue_description:
### 🔎 Search Terms

memory leak, language server, lsp, program clone, ReuseProgram, UpdateProgram, checker pool, retained program, projectReferenceFileMapper, RSS

### 🕗 Version & Regression Information

- This is a memory retention bug in the native (Go) language server (`tsc --lsp`).
- Reproduces on `main` at 87f2e8ca9b.
- I haven't bisected it. It has been present since `projectReferenceFileMapper` started keeping a copy of the full `ProgramOptions`, and the language server started passing `CreateCheckerPool`/`CreateModuleResolver` closures that capture the project.

### ⏯ Playground Link

N/A (language server / memory behavior)

### 💻 Code

Any project with a `tsconfig.json` shows this. Minimal case:

```jsonc
// tsconfig.json
{}
```

```ts
// index.ts
console.log('Hello, world!');
```

Steps:
1. Start `tsc --lsp --stdio` and open `index.ts`.
2. Request diagnostics, hover or completion so the server creates checkers.
3. Edit `index.ts`, for example insert a newline, so the program is updated by cloning (`ProgramUpdateKindCloned`).
4. Wait past the checker idle timeout (30s) and force a GC.
5. The program from before the edit, its checker pool and its checkers are all still reachable.

### 🙁 Actual behavior

After the first edit, the program from before the edit is never garbage collected. Neither are its checker pool or its checkers.

The reference chain is:

```
new Program
  → processedFiles.projectReferenceFileMapper   (shared with every clone by ReuseProgram)
  → opts.CreateCheckerPool                      (closure capturing the *project.Project)
  → old *Project → old Program → old checkerPool → old Checkers
```

`fileLoader.addProjectReferenceTasks` stores the whole `ProgramOptions` on the mapper (`opts: p.opts`). In the language server those options include the `CreateCheckerPool` and `CreateModuleResolver` closures, and both capture the project that created the program. `ReuseProgram` shares `processedFiles`, including the mapper, with every cloned program. So as long as a descendant clone is alive, the original program and everything it created stays reachable, typically until a full program rebuild.

The retained checkers are also never idle-cleaned. Their pool was already `Discard()`ed when the program was replaced, and that stops its idle-cleanup timer.

Measured on a ~500-file Next.js app. A scripted LSP client opened 5 files, requested diagnostics, hover and completion, and made one edit. Heap is `inuse_space` after GC; each figure is the average of 3 runs.

| | observed | with the retention removed |
|---|---|---|
| Go heap, active | ~541 MB | ~464 MB |
| Go heap, idle (after checker idle timeout) | ~471 MB | ~388 MB |
| RSS, idle | ~718 MB | ~600 MB |

I confirmed this with liveness tracking via `runtime.AddCleanup`. After the idle timeout, 2 programs, 2 checker pools and 2 checkers from the pre-edit program were still alive. The expected state is 1 program and 1 pool.

### 🙂 Expected behavior

Once no snapshot references the pre-edit program, it should become unreachable and be garbage collected, together with its checker pool and checkers. Only the current program and its pool should stay alive. This is what `Snapshot.dispose` → `checkerPool.Discard()` is designed for: "allowing the pool and any idle checkers it still references to be reclaimed when the pool is garbage-collected".

### Additional information about the issue

The mapper only reads `opts.Config`, `opts.Host` and `opts.UseSourceOfProjectReference`. It never calls the factory closures, so clearing `CreateCheckerPool` and `CreateModuleResolver` from the copy of the options it keeps breaks the chain without changing behavior.

I have a fix with a regression test. The test edits a file so the program is cloned, then asserts the pre-edit program is garbage collected. It fails before the fix and passes after, and I'm happy to send it as a PR.

Possibly related: microsoft/typescript-go#3032 (LSP memory growth on large projects, root cause never identified).

issue_title: [Bug]: macOS: `ps` prints the published launcher's newlines as `\012`, so `hermes dashboard --status` omits launcher-started backends
issue_description:
## Bug Description

On macOS, every process started through the published POSIX launcher (`<install>/.hermes/bin/hermes`, written by `hermes_cli/_launchers.py::_launcher_script`) runs as `python3 -I -c '<multi-line script>' <subcommand> …`. The `ps`-based readers take that command line from `ps -o command=`, and macOS `ps` prints a newline inside an argument as the four characters `\012` (a tab as `\011`). The canonical matcher never receives the bootstrap source intact, so `_hermes_holder_subcommand()` returns `None` for every launcher-started process.

Effects on a PM install whose LaunchAgents (`ai.hermes.dashboard`, `ai.hermes.serve-desktop`) run the launcher:

- **`hermes dashboard --status` omits the launcher-started dashboard and serve backends.** The spawn-ledger fallback does not rescue them: under the launcher `sys.argv[0]` is `-c`, so the ledger row reads `-c dashboard --host …`, which `_parse_dashboard_runtime()` also rejects. `_report_dashboard_status`'s docstring gives the reason this matters: hiding backends from `--status` "let an operator kill what they couldn't see".
- **The argv captured for the post-update respawn is shredded.** `_dashboard_cmdline_for_pid()` re-splits the `ps` text with shlex. For a live launcher dashboard it returned 70 tokens (`'-c', 'import', 'os,', 're,', 'sys012os.environ.pop(PYTHONHOME,', …`). Replaying that for a manually started backend runs `python3 -I -c import …`, which exits with a SyntaxError. launchd-owned backends are not affected, because they are matched to their job by live PID first.
- **The Desktop-local orphan reaper** (`_reap_orphaned_desktop_local_serves`) cannot see launcher-started `serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0` orphans.
- `hermes update`'s stale-dashboard cleanup still finds launchd backends, through the ledger `purpose` plus the launchd PID (`_find_stale_dashboard_pids(scope_home=…)` returned both PIDs). That path is unaffected.

## Steps to Reproduce

macOS, PM-managed source install:

1. Start a backend through the launcher, e.g. `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/.hermes/bin/hermes dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9119 --no-open`, or through a LaunchAgent whose `ProgramArguments` call it.
2. `ps -p <pid> -o command=` shows `…/python3 -I -c import os, re, sys\012os.environ.pop('PYTHONHOME', None)\012…sys.exit(main())\012 dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9119 --no-open`.
3. `hermes dashboard --status` does not list it.

Smallest repro against a live launcher process:

```python
import subprocess
from hermes_cli.update_cmd_windows import _hermes_holder_subcommand

text = subprocess.run(["ps", "-p", str(pid), "-o", "command="],
                      capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
_hermes_holder_subcommand(text)                         # None
_hermes_holder_subcommand(text.replace("\\012", "\n"))  # 'dashboard'
```

## Expected Behavior

`--status` lists every live dashboard/serve backend, and the argv captured for a respawn is the process's real argv, whichever launcher started it.

## Actual Behavior

Read-only probe with upstream's own matchers against live launchd processes on macOS 26.3.1 (arm64):

| PID | Process | `ps` text as printed | `ps` text, `\012` → newline | psutil `cmdline()` joined |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 83181 | `ai.hermes.dashboard` (`dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9119`) | holder `None`, runtime `None` | holder `dashboard`, runtime `('dashboard', '127.0.0.1', 9119)` | same as decoded |
| 95133 | `ai.hermes.serve-desktop` (`serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9120`) | `None`, `None` | `serve`, `('serve', '127.0.0.1', 9120)` | same |
| 1246 | `ai.hermes.gateway` (`gateway run --external-supervisor`) | `_gateway_command_subcommand` `None`, `looks_like_gateway_command_line` `False` | `run`, `True` | same |
| 804 | launchd `stderr_timestamp` wrapper, parent of 1246 | `None`, `False` | `run`, `True` | same |

Ledger rows `-c dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9119 --no-open` and `-c serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9120 --skip-build`: holder `None`, runtime `None`.

How macOS `ps` renders argv (a Python child started with these arguments):

```text
psutil:          ['a\nb\tc', 'back\\012slash', 'lone\\back', 'cr\rx', 'é']
ps -o command=:  a\012b\011c back\012slash lone\back cr^Mx M-CM-)
```

Tab and newline become `\011` / `\012`. A backslash is not escaped, so a literal `\012` inside an argument looks the same as an encoded newline. CR becomes `^M` and non-ASCII (C locale) becomes `M-…`; neither can be reversed. This matches `strvis(VIS_TAB | VIS_NL | VIS_NOSLASH)`.

## Root Cause Analysis

- **Reader:** `hermes_cli/dashboard_procs.py::_iter_process_table` (`ps -A -o pid=,command=`) returns the vis-encoded text unchanged.
- **Where it fails:** `gateway/status.py::inline_bootstrap_argv` looks for the shortest token run that ends in `)`. The tail token is `sys.exit(main())\012`, so no candidate source is ever tried. Separately, the `"entry"` pattern in `_BOOTSTRAPS` requires `\s` after `import os, re, sys`, and the text has `\012` there. The matcher itself is correct (60e531cb52b was validated on Linux, where `/proc` keeps real newlines); on macOS it just never gets intact source.
- **Per-PID gateway checks are spared:** `_read_process_cmdline()` asks psutil before `ps`, and psutil returns real newlines. That is why the gateway's own identity checks work on this host.

### Gateway: same blind spot, but not safe to fix on its own

- `hermes_cli/gateway.py::_scan_gateway_pids` reads `ps -Aww -o pid=,command=` through `_parse_ps_line` on macOS, so it misses the launcher-started gateway (1246) and its wrapper (804). With a pid file present, `find_gateway_pids()` still finds 1246 through the pid file. Under launch-service a missing pid file is expected (#110166), and then the scan is the only path.
- **Hazard.** `hermes update` runs `_restart_manual_gateways()` after the launchd restarts. It computes `manual_pids = find_gateway_pids(exclude_pids=_get_service_pids(all_profiles=True), all_profiles=True)`. On macOS, `_get_service_pids()` holds the launchd job's own PID. Since the osascript wrapper (`gateway_launchd.launchd_program_arguments`), that PID is `/usr/bin/osascript`, not the gateway. Read-only simulation on this Mac:
  - as shipped: `service_pids=[638]`, `manual_pids=[]`
  - with the `ps` text decoded: `service_pids=[638]`, `manual_pids=[804, 1246]`

  From reading the code, here is what the sweep does with each PID:
  - **1246 (gateway).** Its pid file maps it to the default profile, so it takes `_prepare_profile_gateway_update_restart()`. That returns `"external-supervisor"` because its argv has `--external-supervisor`. The sweep then drains it (SIGUSR1, SIGTERM fallback) and hands it back to launchd, which is a second restart right after launchd's own.
  - **804 (wrapper).** It has no pid-file mapping, so it falls to the unmapped `os.kill(SIGTERM)` branch. The wrapper forwards that signal to the gateway it runs.
  - **Survivors.** `_force_kill_stuck_gateways` SIGKILLs either PID if it is still alive 3 s later.

  In other words, the `\012` blind spot currently shields launchd gateways on PM installs. The simulation covered only the `manual_pids` computation; the per-PID outcomes above come from reading the code.
- Non-PM macOS installs start the wrapper with the single-line `runtime_command` bootstrap, which the scan can already read (checked with the matcher: the wrapper's `runtime_command` and legacy `-m` forms both classify as `gateway run`). Those installs may already hit this sweep. Not reproduced live.
- Suggested order: make `_get_service_pids()` (or the sweep) cover a launchd job's descendants first, then decode `_parse_ps_line` and the `ps` arm of `_read_process_cmdline`. Whether the `stderr_timestamp` wrapper should classify as a gateway at all is a separate question: its argv after `--` is a command it spawns, like the #107002 restart watcher.

### Related gap: the spawn-ledger argv

`process_identity.register_self()` records `" ".join(sys.argv[:10])`, which is `-c dashboard …` under the launcher. `gateway/status.py::_record_argv()` already fixes the same problem for the gateway record (#124029). Wherever the scan misses a backend, `--status` has no parseable fallback. That includes Linux if procps prints control characters as `?`, which is expected from procps but was not verified here. Two options: have `_report_dashboard_status` trust the ledger's structured `purpose`, as it already trusts `_ledger_serve_binds` for host/port, or record the entry-point argv the way `_record_argv()` does.

## Proposed Fix

A fix for the dashboard/serve readers is ready on branch `fix/macos-ps-launcher-cmdline`; I'll link the PR here. It is a bug fix only:

- decode `\011` / `\012` in the `ps` table reader (`_iter_process_table`)
- capture per-PID argv through psutil before `ps` in `_dashboard_cmdline_for_pid`, the same precedence `_read_process_cmdline` already uses
- print each `--status` entry on one line

The gateway readers are intentionally left alone because of the hazard above.

Considered and rejected:

- **Loosening `_BOOTSTRAPS` to accept `\012`.** The fullmatch and both-ends anchoring are what keep a process that merely carries a bootstrap argv (the restart watcher) from matching (#107002). Accepting mangled text there weakens that guard for every reader.
- **Setting `sys.argv[0]` in the launcher.** That change is in-process only and cannot alter the command line `ps` reports.
- **Emitting single-line launcher source.** It does nothing for processes that are already running, republishes every launcher, and leaves the general "an argument contains a newline" class unsolved.

## Duplicates checked

- #124029 (closed): persisted gateway record argv under the launcher, fixed with `_record_argv()`. Different reader.
- #124318 / 60e531cb52b: recognise Hermes inline bootstraps on all OSes. Correct, but on macOS the `ps` readers never hand it intact source.
- #125143 (open, Windows): launcher-respawned gateways fail strict identification. Its proposed patch also parses the command-line string, which on macOS is already mangled, so it would not fix this.
- #75791 (open, Windows): `--status` reports no dashboard on Windows 11. Same symptom, but a different reader (wmic), so it is not this bug.
- #107002: unchanged. This fix works at the reader boundary.
- #92091: scans remain the fallback layer, and this restores that fallback on macOS.

## Environment

- **Affected component:** Other (CLI `dashboard` / `serve` process management and `hermes update`)
- **Operating system:** macOS 26.3.1 (arm64), Darwin 25.3.0
- **Python:** store CPython 3.14.7 (launcher); tests ran on CPython 3.11.15
- **Hermes version:** `v0.21.4+canary.20260928T071354Z-255-ge408d363393` (reproduced). Fix verified on upstream `main` `7c799a6565d` (`-341-g7c799a6565d`). `git diff e408d363393 7c799a6565d` does not touch the affected readers or matchers.
- **Debug report:** not attached. `hermes debug share` uploads config and recent logs to a paste service, and the reproduction above is self-contained (the `ps` rendering plus the canonical matcher). I can provide a redacted `hermes debug share --local` report if it helps.
- **Willing to submit a PR:** yes

issue_title: Suggestion: adopt a documentation format for docstring
issue_description:
As the number of algorithms are increasing, it might make sense to adopt a single documentation format for docstrings. Following are existing currently:
- Google Docstring: https://google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html#s3.8-comments-and-docstrings
- Numpydoc: https://numpydoc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/format.html
- Sphinx: https://sphinx-rtd-tutorial.readthedocs.io/en/latest/docstrings.html

There are editor extensions which help in generating the docstring based on the chosen format like:
- VSCode: https://github.com/NilsJPWerner/autoDocstring

issue_title: intro_sort heap-sort fallback ignores start and end boundaries
issue_description:
### Repository commit

b3f113dc4be16f74be26a5b7a2b89e6419abbfbd

### Python version (python --version)

Python 3.14.7

### Dependencies version (pip freeze)

Not applicable — no third-party dependencies are required. The reproduction uses only Python’s standard library.

### Expected behavior

The `intro_sort()` helper in `sorts/intro_sort.py` should sort only the
half-open range `[start:end]`, leaving elements outside that range unchanged,
including when it switches to heap sort.

Reproduction:

```python
from sorts.intro_sort import intro_sort

values = [100, 4, 3, 2, 1, -100]
result = intro_sort(values, start=1, end=5, size_threshold=2, max_depth=0)
print(result)
```

Expected output:

```text
[100, 1, 2, 3, 4, -100]
```

Only indices 1 through 4 are requested to be sorted. Setting `max_depth=0`
forces the heap-sort fallback.

### Actual behavior

Actual output:

```text
[-100, 1, 2, 3, 4, 100]
```

The heap-sort fallback calls `heap_sort(array)` on the entire list, ignoring
`start` and `end`. Consequently, elements outside the requested range move.

This report concerns range handling in the `intro_sort()` helper. It does
not demonstrate incorrect whole-list ordering from the public `sort()` function.

### Region

Slovakia

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When I use `--download-sections` to grab the first 90 seconds of a YouTube video, the download speed depends on how long the whole video is, not on how much I'm actually downloading.

Short video (3:33, itag 140, ~3.4 MB file):

```
[download] 100% of    1.39MiB in 00:00:00 at 7.57MiB/s
```

Same command, 14-minute video (itag 140, ~13.7 MB file):

```
[download] 100% of    1.39MiB in 00:00:45 at 31.12KiB/s
```

Same 1.39 MiB section, 45 seconds instead of under a second. The cliff is between roughly 11.8 and 11.9 MB - everything above that gets paced at almost exactly 32 KiB/s, everything below is full speed.

What I think is going on: `--download-sections` always goes through the ffmpeg downloader, and ffmpeg opens the googlevideo URL with a single open-ended request. Googlevideo seems to serve response bodies up to ~12 MB at line speed and throttle anything bigger. The native downloader never hits this because it requests bounded chunks.

I checked this with curl on the URL from `yt-dlp -g` (same video, same minute):

```
plain GET             ~32 KB/s                       (throttled)
&range=0-7999999      8,000,000 B in 0.37 s  (~22 MB/s)
&range=0-15999999     ~32 KB/s                       (throttled again above ~12 MB)
```

So bounded `&range=` requests are fine, one big request is not.Things I tried that did not help: `--no-playlist`, a lower-bitrate format (`-f  to bitrate, so it takes just as long), `--http-chunk-size` (ffmpeg downloaderignores it), `--downloader-args "ffmpeg_i:-seekable 1"`, `--hls-prefer-native` . Passing a `Range:` header via `--downloader-args ffmpeg_i:-headers` gave me a4xx from googlevideo.

issue_title: url_or_none rejects URLs with uppercase schemes
issue_description:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues for similar reports.
- [x] This is a self-contained utility bug report, not a site-specific extraction failure.

### Description

`yt_dlp.utils.url_or_none` currently rejects URLs whose scheme contains uppercase letters:

```py
>>> from yt_dlp.utils import url_or_none
>>> url_or_none('HTTP://example.com/video.mp4')
None
```

URL schemes are case-insensitive, so this should be accepted the same way as the lowercase form:

```py
>>> url_or_none('http://example.com/video.mp4')
'http://example.com/video.mp4'
```

This can matter when extractors receive URLs directly from metadata or manifests without normalizing the scheme first.

### Expected behavior

`url_or_none('HTTP://example.com/video.mp4')` returns the stripped URL.

### Actual behavior

It returns `None`.

issue_title: Postgres node: a comma in a query-parameter value is split into several bind values
issue_description:
> **⚠️ Severity corrected after further testing.** An earlier version of this report
> claimed *silent data corruption*. That was wrong: I had verified n8n's value
> **collection** but not the value **binding**. Supplying the surplus value to
> PostgreSQL produces a hard error, not a wrong write. See the
> [correction comment](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/40022#issuecomment-5919564259).
> The code path and the fix suggestion are unchanged.

**Affected version:** 2.41.3 — and current `master`. The code is byte-identical in both
(verified against `n8n@2.41.3` and `master`: same statements, same line numbers).
**Node version:** `typeVersion` 2.5 and above, i.e. the current branch.
**Impact:** the query fails with a parameter-count error that does not point at the real
cause. No incorrect data is written.

## Summary

The Postgres node tells users to use `$1, $2, …` with **Query Parameters** to avoid SQL
injection. When a parameter's evaluated value is a **string containing a comma that is not
itself valid JSON**, the node splits that one value into several bind values. The
resulting parameter count no longer matches the statement, and execution fails with an
error that blames the *count* rather than the comma in the user's data.

## Affected code

`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Postgres/v2/actions/database/executeQuery.operation.ts`,
inside the `nodeVersion >= 2.5` branch (lines 106–108 in both 2.41.3 and `master`):

```ts
const evaluatedExpression = evaluateExpression(rawEvaluated);
const evaluatedValues = isJSON(evaluatedExpression)
    ? [evaluatedExpression]
    : stringToArray(evaluatedExpression);

if (evaluatedValues.length) values.push(...evaluatedValues);
```

`stringToArray` (`helpers/utils.ts`) is a comma split with empty filtering and trimming:

```ts
export function stringToArray(str: NodeParameterValueType | undefined) {
	if (str === undefined) return [];
	return String(str)
		.split(',')
		.filter((entry) => entry)
		.map((entry) => entry.trim());
}
```

So a single parameter whose evaluated value is `O'Brien, Test` contributes **two** bind
values instead of one.

## Why `isJSON()` does not save you

`evaluateExpression` (`helpers/utils.ts`) returns plain strings via `toString()` — it does
**not** JSON-encode them:

```ts
return typeof expression === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(expression) : expression.toString();
```

So `isJSON()` returns `true` only when the *data itself* happens to parse as JSON:

| evaluated value | `isJSON` | bind values produced | correct? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `123` | true | 1 | yes |
| `true` | true | 1 | yes |
| `Doe, John` | **false** | **2** | **no** |
| `O'Brien, Test` | **false** | **2** | **no** |
| `hello, world, again` | **false** | **3** | **no** |

This is why casual testing tends to pass: a numeric or boolean-looking value behaves
correctly, while ordinary free text does not. It is **data-dependent**, which is the most
dangerous shape for a bug in a form/webhook ingestion path.

## Reproduction

1. Add a **Postgres** node, operation **Execute Query**, with **Query Parameters** on.
2. Query: `SELECT $1::text AS a, $2::text AS b` — two placeholders.
3. Query parameters, in the node's `options.queryReplacement`:
   - `={{ $json.name }}`
   - `={{ $json.note }}`
4. Feed webhook/Code-node data: `{ "name": "Doe, John", "note": "hello" }`
5. Execute.

### Verified — value collection, using the node's own logic

`isJSON`, `evaluateExpression` and `stringToArray` copied verbatim from `helpers/utils.ts`,
plus the `nodeVersion >= 2.5` branch copied verbatim, mocking only `getResolvables()` and
the expression evaluator. Observed bind values:

```
no commas   {name:"Smith",      note:"hello"}                 -> ["Smith","hello"]           correct
comma in $1 {name:"Doe, John", note:"hello"}                 -> ["Doe","John","hello"]       3 values, 2 placeholders
3 params    {name:"Doe, John", note:"hello", city:"Galena"}   -> ["Doe","John","hello","Galena"]  4 values, 3
legacy <2.5 {name:"Doe, John", note:"hello"}                 -> ["Doe, John","hello"]         SAFE
array       {tags:["a","b","c"]}                             -> ["a","b","c"]                 #31704 fix present
```

### Verified — what the database then does

```
BEGIN;
CREATE TEMP TABLE reprobind (a text, b text);
PREPARE two (text, text) AS INSERT INTO reprobind VALUES ($1, $2) RETURNING a, b;
EXECUTE two('Doe', 'John', 'hello');
```
```
ERROR:  wrong number of parameters for prepared statement "two"
DETAIL:  Expected 2 parameters but got 3.
```

The driver rejects the surplus value; it does not drop it and does not shift the remaining
bindings.

**This can never be silent.** `stringToArray` splits on commas and filters empties, so a
value containing a comma can only ever *add* to the parameter count, never reduce it.
`values.length` is therefore always `>=` the number of expressions supplied, so the count
either overshoots the placeholders (*"Expected N but got M"*) or undershoots them (the
mirror error). It can never accidentally re-align.

## Note on the `nodeVersion < 2.5` branch

The older branch splits the **raw** parameter string (`rawReplacements.replace(/^=+/, '').split(',')`)
and then pushes each *evaluated* result **whole**:

```ts
for (const rawValue of rawValues) {
    const resolvables = getResolvables(rawValue);
    if (resolvables.length) {
        for (const resolvable of resolvables) {
            values.push(this.evaluateExpression(`${resolvable}`, index) as IDataObject);
        }
    } else {
        values.push(rawValue);
    }
}
```

Because the split is applied *before* evaluation, commas inside the **data** are safe
there. The hazard is in the newer branch, where the split is applied *after* evaluation.

## Relationship to #30978 / #31704

#30978 reported that a JS **array** was wrapped as a single bind value because of the same
`isJSON()` mismatch, and #31704 (merged 2026-06-04) fixed it by spreading arrays. That fix
handles `Array.isArray(rawEvaluated)` and does not change the `isJSON() ? … : stringToArray(…)`
path for **strings**, so the comma case described here remains. This looks like the
remaining half of the same underlying problem: the node cannot reliably distinguish "a
string that is one value" from "a comma-separated list of values".

## Suggested fix

Keep the ability to pass several literal parameters, but never split a value that came
from an expression. Concretely, in the `nodeVersion >= 2.5` branch, when the raw parameter
contained a resolvable, push the evaluated result as exactly one value, and reserve
`stringToArray` for parameters that are literal text with no `{{ }}`:

```ts
if (resolvables.length) {
    for (const resolvable of resolvables) {
        const rawEvaluated = this.evaluateExpression(`${resolvable}`, index);
        if (Array.isArray(rawEvaluated)) {
            for (const item of rawEvaluated) { /* unchanged */ }
            continue;
        }
        // an expression evaluates to exactly one value
        values.push(evaluateExpression(rawEvaluated));
    }
} else {
    values.push(...stringToArray(rawValues));
}
```

If comma-splitting of *literal* parameters must be preserved for backwards compatibility,
that is the branch to keep it in. The current behaviour appears to be unintentional: a
single expression is expected to yield a single bind value everywhere else in the node.

Happy to open a PR with tests if that is useful.

## Environment

- n8n 2.41.3, self-hosted
- Postgres node `typeVersion` 2.5
- Observed on a form/webhook ingestion workflow storing free-text customer input

issue_title: boundImages recomputes the strip set per request — stripped images flip back to live and invalidate the prompt cache
issue_description:
## Summary

`boundImages()` (`packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts`, since v2.0.x) recomputes which inline images to strip **from scratch on every request**. When the history changes (a new image arrives, compaction prunes, tool output is truncated), the total image bytes move around the 25 MiB trigger and previously-stripped images **flip back to live**. That rewrites the prompt prefix at the oldest image's position, so every provider-side prompt cache behind it is discarded — in our case a ~300k-token conversation re-prefilled on every turn after a few screenshots were read, including plain-text turns.

## Evidence

With a local inference server that logs cache reuse, the divergence is exactly at the position of the first stripped image: consecutive requests alternate between the image payload and the `IMAGE_REMOVED` placeholder at the same token offset (`image_pad` vs placeholder text), and cache reuse collapses from ~99.9% to the system-prompt root each time. On our backend (strata, a custom llama.cpp-derived server with a conversation KV cache) this forces a **full re-prefill of the entire KV cache** — every turn after a few screenshots, including plain-text turns, pays ~300k tokens of prefill (~30–40 s) that the cache should have served.

## Why it's a bug, not a policy question

The strip policy (25 MiB trigger → 15 MiB target) is untouched. The issue is that the *decision* is non-monotonic: the same message renders differently across requests, which silently breaks prefix caching for every provider. A one-way decision fixes it without changing when stripping happens.

## Proposed fix

Make the strip decision sticky per image (content hash + occurrence index, so identical-but-distinct attachments stay distinct): once an image is replaced by the placeholder, it stays replaced for the process lifetime. Stripping still only starts above the trigger and winds down to the target.

Author: hermes <hermes@local>
Date:   Mon Oct 5 15:09:49 2026 +0800

    fix(session): make boundImages stripping sticky per image
    
    Recomputing the strip set per request let a stripped image flip back to
    live whenever the history changed, rewriting the prompt prefix at the
    image position and discarding the provider prompt cache behind it. The
    decision is now one-way, keyed by content hash + occurrence.

+// and discarding the provider's prompt cache for the whole conversation behind it. The decision is
+// one-way: once stripped, an image stays stripped for the life of the process.

+// A stable identity for an image payload: mime, length, and sampled bytes. Identical bytes across

+}
+

   // Remote and provider-referenced media carry no local payload and never count toward the inline budget.
@@ -166,33 +192,58 @@ export const boundImages = (messages: LLMRequest["messages"]) => {

-    (total, message) =>

-        if (part.type !== "tool-result" || part.result.type !== "content") return sum
-        return (
-          sum +

-            (bytes: number, item: Content) =>
-              bytes + (item.type === "file" && isImage(item.mime) ? Buffer.byteLength(item.uri) : 0),
-            0,
-          )
-        )
-      }, 0),
-    0,
-  )
-  if (imageBytes <= IMAGE_BYTES_TRIGGER) return messages
+  const uriSize = (uri: string) => Buffer.byteLength(uri)
+
+  // Identical payloads are distinct attachments, so each occurrence of a hash gets its own key.
+  const occurrence = () => {
+    const seen = new Map<string, number>()
+    return (base: string) => {
+      const n = seen.get(base) ?? 0

-        if (part.type === "media" && isImage(part.media.mediaType) && imageBytes - removed > IMAGE_BYTES_TARGET) {

-          return Message.text(IMAGE_REMOVED)

+          const key = placed(mediaSample(part.media))
+          if (strippedImages.has(key)) {
+            changed = true
+            return Message.text(IMAGE_REMOVED)
+          }
+          if (shouldStrip()) {
+            strippedImages.add(key)
+            budget -= size(part.media)
+            changed = true
+            return Message.text(IMAGE_REMOVED)
+          }
+          return part
         }
         if (part.type !== "tool-result" || part.result.type !== "content") return part
         return {
@@ -200,15 +251,27 @@ export const boundImages = (messages: LLMRequest["messages"]) => {

issue_title: npm 12 upgrade leaves the Windows executable stub
issue_description:
### Description

`opencode upgrade` can report success with npm 12 while leaving the published text stub in `bin/opencode.exe`. The next invocation fails on Windows because the file is not a valid executable.

The updater runs `npm install --global --force` without allowing the target package's lifecycle scripts. npm 12 can block postinstall and still exit 0, even with `ignore-scripts=false`. Adding `--allow-scripts=@opencode/cli` lets postinstall replace the stub.

I reproduced that policy behavior with a synthetic package in an isolated Windows install prefix using npm 12.0.2 and Node 24.21.0. The flag also preserved explicit `ignore-scripts=true`. This report covers the updater command; #48884 covers the broader packaging behavior when scripts are disabled.

### OpenCode version

Reported on the upgrade from 2.0.16 to 2.0.18.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start with a working npm installation of OpenCode 2.0.16 and npm 12.0.2, with `ignore-scripts=false` and no script approval for `@opencode/cli`.
2. Run `opencode upgrade 2.0.18` using the npm method.
3. Run `opencode --version`.

The upgrade reports success, but Windows rejects `bin/opencode.exe`. Running the installed package's `postinstall.mjs` manually repairs it.

### Operating System

Windows

GitLab Duo workflow models do not work correctly with a self-managed GitLab instance.

I found two issues while testing this:

2. If the stored GitLab OAuth token is expired and the refresh fails, provider initialization throws and can prevent OpenCode from starting.

2. Authenticate OpenCode with GitLab OAuth and configure GitLab Duo.

3. Start OpenCode using the GitLab Duo workflow model:
   ```powershell
   opencode -m gitlab/duo-workflow`

4. On a self-managed GitLab instance, start a GitLab Duo workflow and observe that the workflow does not receive the working directory and project/namespace context required for the current repository.

5. Let the stored GitLab OAuth credentials expire or make the refresh token invalid/revoked, then start OpenCode again.

6. OpenCode attempts to refresh the expired GitLab OAuth token. If GitLab returns `invalid_grant`, provider initialization throws and OpenCode can fail to start.

issue_title: notFound() serves an empty `__next_error__` document instead of not-found.tsx
issue_description:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/franknoel/next-notfound-ssr

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction and run `npm install`.
2. Run `npm run build && npm run start` (`npm run dev` shows the same thing).
3. Run `./check.sh`, or fetch the pages by hand:

```sh
curl -s http://localhost:3000/missing        # page that calls notFound()
curl -s http://localhost:3000/no/such/route  # URL that matches no route
```

The app has three files: a root layout with `<html lang="en">`, an `app/not-found.tsx` that renders `NOT FOUND BOUNDARY`, and `app/[slug]/page.tsx`, which calls `notFound()` unless the slug is `known`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** `/missing` answers 404, but its HTML is `<html id="__next_error__"><head></head><body>` plus scripts. The root layout does not render, so there is no `lang` and none of the `not-found.tsx` markup. That markup exists only in the RSC payload, so the page is blank until it hydrates, and stays blank without JavaScript.

An unmatched URL (`/no/such/route`) is fine: it renders `not-found.tsx` inside the root layout.

`check.sh` output, the same on 16.3.6 and 16.4.0-canary.48, in `next dev` and in `next build && next start`:

```
/known           200  <html lang="en">             boundary/page text in HTML: yes
/missing         404  <html id="__next_error__">   boundary/page text in HTML: no
/no/such/route   404  <html lang="en">             boundary/page text in HTML: yes
```

**Expected:** `/missing` renders like `/no/such/route`: the root layout with `NOT FOUND BOUNDARY` in the server HTML, and the same 404 status.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.6.0: Tue Aug 18 17:49:13 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.161.15.700.19~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
  Available memory (MB): 32768
  Available CPU cores: 10
Binaries:
  Node: 24.21.0
  npm: 11.19.0
  Yarn: 1.22.22
  pnpm: 9.15.9
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.6 // Latest available version is detected (16.3.6).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.2.8
  react-dom: 19.2.8
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Not Found, Error Handling

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), next build (local), next start (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

Also reproduces on `next@16.4.0-canary.48`, dev and prod.

Same bug as #98295 and #98954, which were closed automatically for lacking a reproduction link.

Where it seems to happen: `HTTPAccessFallbackBoundary` is a client error boundary, and React does not run error boundaries during server rendering, so the `notFound()` throw escapes the Fizz shell. The catch in `app-render` (`renderToStream`, and `prerenderToStream` for ISR) sets the 404 status and renders `getErrorRSCPayload`, whose seed is the hardcoded `__next_error__` document. Because the status and the empty document come from the same catch, an app cannot get a 404 with real HTML from `notFound()`.

We hit it on a site with locale-prefixed routes: every unknown page and event URL is served without `lang` or any text.

Zstandard ([RFC 8878](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8878)) is well-positioned to replaced GZIP ([RFC 1952](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1952)) as the de-facto compression format.

Zstandard:
* is [faster to compress/decompress](https://facebook.github.io/zstd/#benchmarks) than GZIP,
* has [much better compression ratios](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/62446#issue-1880889127),
* is [well-specified](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8878), 
* is [backed by a prominent company](https://github.com/facebook/zstd), and 
* is seeing increased adoption in use with archives and as a [browser content encoding](https://chromestatus.com/feature/6186023867908096).
 
Given the likely ubiquitous place Zstandard is going have in the future, I propose first-class adoption of Zstandard in the stdlib.

Existing Go implementations:
* @klauspost has an excellent Zstandard implementation at [github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd), but the API is a somewhat complex and it makes use of native assembly.
* @ianlancetaylor implemented a Zstandard decompressor in [internal/zstd](https://github.com/golang/go/tree/master/src/internal/zstd) without any use of `unsafe` or assembly.

Some goals for this package:
* The API be simple and similar to existing packages like `compress/gzip`.
* It does not use `unsafe` or assembly similar to the existing compress package.
  * Performance is always nice, but Go community surveys consistently shows security as more important than performance.
  * Users who just need a decently fast enough Zstandard implementation can use `compress/zstd`, while those want the best performance and/or advanced features of Zstandard can use @klauspost's package. Any stdlib packages (e.g., `net/http` that make use of `compress/zstd` should make it possible to swap over to a different `zstd` implementation).
  * Note that the same is already true of `compress/gzip`, which is generally good enough (although there is still room for performance optimizations), but power users can use [github.com/klauspost/compress/gzip](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/klauspost/compress/gzip), which is much faster (as it makes use of assembly).

We could:
* adopt @klauspost's pure-Go (i.e., no assembly) implementation with a cleaned-up API
* extend @ianlancetaylor's work to support compressing
* do a combination of both

Related issues:
* #62492
* #55107
* #62446

set GOTELEMETRY=local
